18_marg3: IN THE FIRST YEAR OF CYRUS. As Cyrus, the empire of the Chaldeans being destroyed, freed the people of God, sent them back to their homeland, commanded the burnt temple to be rebuilt in Jerusalem, and made this edict known also by letters, so Christ, the kingdom of the devil being destroyed, gathered into the Church his elect who had been scattered by his tyranny; which, justified now by faith, has peace with God through him and hastens to the vision of everlasting peace, for Jerusalem is called 'vision of peace'. He also has the burnt temple restored, when, leading back to salvation those who had lost the faith through the snares of the devil, he makes them worthy of his dwelling; he also sends the sacred and holy Scriptures through the whole world, by which he preaches faith in his name and the hope of salvation to all who belong to his kingdom, that is, to the elect.
18_interl5: because then he had no adversary, or, the empire of the Chaldeans being destroyed, he believed that no one could resist him; so too Christ says: "All power is given to me in heaven and in earth"
18_interl6: he confesses the God of Israel to be the God of heaven, and acknowledges also that he has all the kingdoms of the earth in his power and can give them to whom he will
18_marg4: BEDE. Each of the doctors, and the whole Church together, is wont to be called in the holy Scriptures the house or temple of God, because he is wont to dwell in the hearts of those who believe, hope and love; whence: "If any one love me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him" etc. Hence the Apostle himself also says: "The temple of God is holy, which you are." And elsewhere: "But Christ as the Son in his own house: which house are we" etc. In figure of this spiritual house or temple Solomon made the temple to the Lord in Jerusalem. For he is interpreted 'peaceable', figuring him of whom it is said: "His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace"; of whom the Apostle says: "And coming, he preached peace to you that were afar off, and peace to them that were nigh" etc. And that he built the temple in seven years, but finished and dedicated it in the eighth, signifies that through the whole time of this world, which runs round in seven days, the Lord builds the Church, the faithful being gathered for the heavenly building, and in the future life, when the glory of the resurrection appears, he perfects it wholly and raises it into the joy of immortal life in the eternal brightness of his vision; for because he himself rose on the eighth day, that is, after the seventh of the sabbath, the time of our resurrection too is rightly expressed by the number eight. And that in the following age certain buildings of the temple began to be decayed by age, but were restored by the diligence of kings and priests, signifies the daily errors of the faithful, of which it is said: "A just man shall fall seven times and shall rise again"; who are corrected by the daily skill of the times through the examples or exhortations of the just who went before, as it were by the industry of the priests and kings of God. For all the perfect are called kings and priests, since they are members of the supreme King and Priest, and have learned to rule themselves well and to present their bodies a living sacrifice to God. That afterwards, as evils increased, the temple was profaned by the filth of idols and at last destroyed and burnt by the Chaldeans, signifies the graver falls of those who, united to the members of the Church by the confession of right faith and the sacrament of baptism, are again, by the fraud of demons, cast down from the state of faith and burnt with the flame of vices. That, when the temple and the city of Jerusalem were destroyed, its citizens were removed into Babylon, but after seventy years, having done penance, were sent back to their homeland by the Lord's mercy and again restored the temple and the holy city with great labour, signifies those who, deceived by the devil, lose not only the sincerity of faith and the integrity of good work, but also by the bitterness of their crimes are made like gentiles and publicans, whence: "Let him be to thee as the heathen and publican"; [some] of whom, pricked to the heart by the illumination of the Holy Spirit, again hear and keep the commandments of God which they had left. For there are seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, and the sum of the divine law is comprised in ten commandments, and ten times seven are seventy. Hence fittingly those who had been taken captive into Babylonia through perverse works are freed after seventy years and rebuild the house of God and the holy city; because sometimes those who, separated by their sins from the communion of the Church, were joined to the number of unbelievers, again through the gift of the Holy Spirit exercise good works, and so recover the fellowship of the faithful, that is, of the house and city of God, from which they had been cast out. For it is to be noted that the house of the Lord rebuilt after the burning, the city restored, the people sent back to their homeland after the captivity, and the holy vessels brought back, all proclaim the same return of penitents to the Church. But because Esdras unfolds all these things, it is pleasing to expound some things from his volume in a spiritual sense, that it may be made clearer how those who had perished through negligence or error must return to penance; with how great grace of God, with how great effort of their own, pardon for what they have committed must be sought and obtained; how the penitent, with those who have lately come to the faith, build the same house of Christ, and together await in the future the solemnities of its dedication.
18_marg5: BEDE. In these words the great faith and great piety of the king shine forth. Faith indeed, because he understood that the people of Israel was God's before others. Piety, because he allowed all who wished, none excepted, to return free to their homeland. Faith, in that he confessed that the same God both dwells in the heavens and is in Jerusalem, and can go up with each of those returning. For it is plain that he believed him to be not bodily and contained in a place, but a spirit and present everywhere, whom he confessed so to have a place in Jerusalem and in the temple that he did not doubt that he at the same time presides over the kingdom of heaven; he believed him so to reign in the heavens that he is with his faithful on earth and directs their minds and hands to saving works.
18_interl7: as it were: he is not bodily nor contained in a place
18_interl9: otherwise no one can pass from the confusion of sins to the works of the virtues, that is, from the bondage of Babylon to the freedom of the homeland
18_interl10: that is, in confession; that those who through forgetfulness of God are taken captive by the Chaldeans, that is, by the demons, may return through the confession of the divine goodness to the vision of peace and light
18_marg6: BEDE. Those who sin or care for worldly things are below; those who desire to please God sigh for heavenly things; let them pass beyond all the pomps and allurements of the world through love of eternal things, and build a house to God in Judea, that is, in the confession of their own iniquity and of the divine mercy; let them prepare their hearts, which God may deign to inhabit and enlighten, and strive by words and examples to invite their neighbours to the same.
18_interl11: the rich, namely, who cannot preach
18_interl12: either in Chaldea, that is, or scattered elsewhere through fear of the Chaldeans
18_marg7: The distinction of the words is to be noted: for the king gave leave to all who were released from captivity, that whoever would might go up, with the Lord as leader, to build the temple; yet he did not command all to go up, but those whom, liberty being granted, it pleased to dwell elsewhere he commanded each from his own place to help those going up, namely by giving them money or cattle for the needs of so long a journey; he also desired them to give and entrust to them other gifts, which they should offer in the temple of the Lord as a memorial of the senders. All therefore were freed from captivity, all were given to works of piety, but the more perfect went up to build the temple to the Lord, the rest helped. For all the elect, rescued from the power of darkness, belong to the freedom of the sons of God and of glory; all rejoice to be numbered in the society of the holy city, that is, of the Church; but it belongs only to the perfect to labour in the building of that same Church by preaching also to others, who are given double honour by the Apostle, as the angel says to Daniel: "They that are learned shall shine as the brightness of the firmament: and they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity." For the instructors of many, the more they train their hearers to love heavenly things, the less care they take for earthly things; nay, they leave what they have acquired for the hope of eternal things. Hence it is necessary that the rich, who cannot preach, stand by to relieve their want for preaching, that so they may be partakers of the preaching. Whence John: "We therefore ought to receive such, that we may be fellow helpers of the truth."
18_marg8: Those who abound in temporal things ought not only to minister necessaries to the poor of Christ, but also willingly to do for themselves what good they can, that by both benefits they may deserve to have a part in the temple of God, which is the Church.
18_interl15: because they lie with a weak and sluggish mind, or have no care for their own or their brethren's love and salvation
18_marg9: Cyrus commanded all, or rather permitted [all], to go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the Lord; but only those of Juda and Benjamin and the tribe of Levi were willing to go up. For the ten tribes under king Jeroboam were estranged from the temple of God and the worship of piety, and therefore were [taken] into captivity by the kings of the Assyrians, nor, as they relate, did they ever all come into their homeland. But Juda and Benjamin and the tribe of Levi, to which the ministry of the temple belonged, although they imitated the sins of the ten tribes, never deserted the dwelling of the city and the ceremonies of the temple. Hence they were both taken last by the Chaldeans and allowed to return first under the reign of the Persians, because, namely, our Lord was born of the tribe of Juda and of Levi. The tribe of Benjamin also joined itself to them in religious faith, chiefly because Jerusalem was in its lot, and therefore it deserved to be partaker of the mercy bestowed.
18_interl16: by admonishing through the Scriptures and pouring in grace
18_marg10: For it belongs to the chief of the fathers, that is, to the masters, by work and teaching to build up the minds of those who err in the pursuit of good work.
18_marg11: Scribes instructed in the kingdom of heaven, who, skilfully examining the merits and understanding of their hearers, know how to judge whom to promote and to what grade of ecclesiastical ministry.
18_marg12: By daily advances, as by certain steps, one ascends to the summit of the virtues, which are in the vision of eternal peace. The first steps are to correct one's own life; the second, to labour over the errors of one's neighbours; the highest, after good works and teaching, to await the joys of everlasting reward.
18_interl17: the rich, awaiting the joys of everlasting reward
18_marg13: Companions who cannot build help the hands of the builders by giving money, when laymen commit their children or household to the preachers to be brought up for the Lord, that what they cannot do by themselves they may offer to the Lord as the gift of their devotion through those who can.
18_interl19: [men] illustrious in natural wit, shining with polished [so the edition: 'fixis'] eloquence
18_marg14: BEDE. That is, the slower, but gentle for bearing the light yoke of the gospel. They give also cattle, namely the humble in spirit and the meek, who give freely to the poor of their substance as of milk and wool. They give both substance and divers furniture, when they commend to the doctors men or women distinguished with manifold flowers of works, parents or members of their household, through whom they may be consecrated to the Lord and advance in the building of the house of the Lord. For there are very many who by natural gift are chaste, patient, modest, liberal, lovers of justice and wisdom, instant in prayers and alms like Cornelius, and "who have not the law, do by nature those things that are of the law". When these are offered to the holy preachers to be born again in Christ or to be confirmed in the faith, they are given to the chief of the fathers as divers furniture for building the house of the Lord.
18_interl21: any unclean spirit whatever, which snatches the faithful from the Church and deprives them of the joy of eternal peace
18_interl22: by joining them to the fellowship of the reprobate, who are the temple and city of the devil their head, that is, of all evil angels and men
18_marg15: BEDE. The divers kinds of vessels signify the divers persons or prayers of the faithful. In the Apocalypse we read that "the four and twenty ancients had golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints". For vials are open and bright vessels, and signify the hearts of the simple, which have nothing of crafty thought, but bring forth with a pure tongue what they hold in their heart. In such, then, perfumes, that is, prayers acceptable to God, are related to be. The knives, which they used for cutting or dividing with fitting reason the limbs of the victims, so that, all being distinguished by reason, part was consumed on the altar, part given to the priests, part to the Levites, part to the offerers, signify those who have discretion, who know perfectly how to discern concerning the saving sacrifice, which is Christ, what is to be said to all, what to the more perfect, what, exceeding the measure of human thought, is to be given to the fire of the Holy Spirit. The golden cups [are] those who glow with the greater splendour of wisdom; but the silver ones those who, ruddy [so the edition: 'rutili'] with the beauty of teaching, expound more plainly what they know; distinguishing whom the Apostle says: "To one indeed, by the Spirit, is given the word of wisdom: and to another, the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit." And that the number of the vessels is recorded both specially for each and generally in the sum of all signifies that the Lord holds written in the book of eternal memory the sum of his elect, not only of those who persevere in the cleanness of faith, but also of those who return to the faith by coming to their senses; in figure of whom it is fittingly added: Sassabasar took all etc.
18_marg16: This is done when Christ, who is the heir of all whom he predestined to salvation, rescues them from the power of Satan and offers them to the priests of the Church to be reconciled through penance.

18_interl25: who know how to divide and understand with discretion the sacrifice which is Christ
18_marg17: Because the Lord knows the number of the elect, nor does any of his sheep perish that confess his great and terrible name.
18_marg18: Because none of the predestined can perish for ever; for if at any time they are carried off into Babylon, that is, into the confusion of sins, by divine providence they are brought back through the fellowship of the just to the peace of the Church. But the vessels which the army of the Chaldeans, when Jerusalem was taken, is related to have broken and, broken, carried into Babylonia, express those who are so taken by the devil that, before they repent, they are snatched away to everlasting punishment.
18_interl26: who, with fervent charity, are wont to be inebriated with consolations
18_marg19: Of Judea, that is, not of Babylonia. For to it belonged also those of the stock of the captives born in Babylonia. For they sighed with their whole soul for Judea and Jerusalem; whose figure their leader Zorobabel bears, who by his very name shows himself born in Babylon, but by intention and work a citizen of Jerusalem. In a higher sense the children of the Church are children of the heavenly homeland, not only those who are already imbued with the sacraments of the Church, but also those who, outside, that is, at times wandering among the impious, are by divine election foreordained to life before the ages and are to be consecrated by the ministries of divine grace; of whom it is well added: And they returned to Jerusalem.
18_marg20: For when, freed from the power of Satan, those who had strayed from the faith, together with those who have lately learned the faith, have returned to Jerusalem of the longed-for peace and to Judea of confession or praise, each one soon seeks again and enters his own city, that is, devoutly carries out the keeping and practice of the virtues which the divine favour bestows according to the measure of faith. And well, when he had said generally that they returned to Juda and Jerusalem, he added: every one to his own city; because each so dwelt in his own city that all in general belonged to Juda and Jerusalem. Jerusalem therefore designates the universal state of the Church, and the cities belonging to it the several virtues of the faithful, in which they are defended from the attacks of demons. By the cities in which those dwelt who had come from captivity to Jerusalem and Judea can also be taken the divers churches throughout the world, of which the one catholic [Church] is made up; in which whoever live each profess themselves sons of the catholic Church, as it were citizens of Jerusalem. And before the others they had Zorobabel and Josue as leaders, of whom one was of the royal, the other of the priestly stock, who bore the one person of the true King and High Priest. He alone it is through whom we come to salvation, whence: "No man cometh to the Father, but by me"; who gathers each of the elect, either by himself through hidden inspiration or through preachers by open teaching, from the confusion of the present life to the vision of peace and the confession of divine praise, as it were to Judea and Jerusalem from Babylon. And the vision of peace and confession is begun in the present and perfected in the future.
18_marg21: BEDE. Scripture therefore carefully distinguished from which generation of the captives they were released and returned to their homeland, that they might be admonished from this with how great certainty the Lord writes the sum of his elect in the book of life, and as it were marks down in the register of heaven how many souls each of the faithful converted by word or example, for whom he will reward them with a sure recompense.
18_marg22: BEDE. By the people of Israel he means the tribe of Juda and Benjamin, and whoever of the other tribes had once escaped the hands of the Assyrians but had been [carried] into captivity with these by the Babylonians. Finally it is to be noted that in the very order of the catalogue, and more where the same catalogue is repeated in the second part of the book, that is, in the words of Nehemias, the names of about fifteen cities are inserted which, unless I am mistaken, are found only in Juda and Benjamin. Hence it is probable that the people of Israel in this place is to be understood chiefly of these tribes, together with the priests and Levites who had had a lot among them.
18_interl28: in very many [manuscripts] it is lacking
18_marg23: BEDE. The Nathinites, who are described in order after the priests, Levites, singers and porters, were then those who are now called subdeacons in the Church, obeying the offices of the Levites and receiving the offerings from the people in the temple.
18_interl44: these were the stewards [so the edition: 'auctores'] of the temple, who repaired the roofs if by chance they had been damaged, and restored them out of the sacred money
18_marg24: In this place, even according to the letter, the grace of God is shown, by which even in the Old Testament gentiles were received to salvation; for when the catalogue of those who were certainly known to belong truly to the people of God had been set out, those were added of whom it was not known whether they were of Israel or of the proselytes, and their number is set out together among the sons of Israel. For although, through the long separation of their fathers from the temple or people of God, they could not show how they belonged to it, yet because they had gone up from the captivity when general leave was given, they were received as companions; for the rest of the Israelites rejoiced to have them as brothers and acquaintances for love of the common faith and religion, even if they knew them less in the origin of the flesh. Allegorically, among the penitents who, freed from the captivity of vices, go up to build the house of the Lord in themselves or in others, there are some who, bound by very many graver sins, seem so estranged by God from every act of piety and chastity that nothing at all of the goodness and religion which they had received from the doctors seems to have remained in them; nor can they show whether they were begotten of Israel, that is, of holy Church, because by sinning such men have become as if they had never belonged to the Holy Spirit; yet by repenting they are corrected and converted, so that their number is written in heaven among the true Israelites in whom there is no guile.
18_marg25: AND OF THE CHILDREN OF THE PRIESTS. BEDE. The children of the transmigration act with the same caution toward the priests as toward the people. For they took care that it should be distinctly clear who truly belonged to the people of Israel or to the priestly race, and who were either suspect or certainly begotten of the stock of proselytes, that is, of strangers. The suspect priests therefore they removed from the office of the altar until their origin should be more certainly made clear; but nonetheless they kept them in the fellowship of those who returned with unanimous peace. Mystically, the sons of the priests going up from the Babylonian captivity seek the writing of their genealogy and, not finding it, are cast out of the priesthood, when ministers of the altar fall into such great crimes or wicked doctrines that, even if by repenting they return to the salvation of the soul, they are not worthy to be restored to the sacred grade. For although among the faithful they await eternal life, yet they do not find among the perfect priests the writing of their grade, which they cannot regain.
18_interl46: "The multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul"
18_interl48: although so great an army, of such divers grades, such divers conditions
18_marg26: ALL THE MULTITUDE etc. BEDE. These signify those who strive by the progress of a more amended life to overcome vices and climb to the summit of the virtues, yet are not yet sufficient of themselves to provide the way of the regular life, but are restrained and directed by the diligence of those who have gone before in Christ.
18_interl50: who sounded the psalms with sweet melody, which the Levites did in the temple among the daily sacrifices, which it is credible that many of the people also did in their own places
18_marg27: BEDE. Mystically, in the temple or people of God the singers are those who keep the heavenly commandments with greater sweetness of mind and commit them to their hearers to be kept with frequent exhortations. And well are singing women joined to the singers because of sex, namely the feminine, in which very many persons are found who not only by living but also by preaching kindle the hearts of their neighbours to the praise of their Creator, and as it were with the sweetness of their voice help those building the temple.
18_marg28: BEDE. The mule is begotten of an ass and a mare, the she-mule of a horse and a she-ass. Among the men who had gone up from the captivity the animals by which they were helped are also described, and their number is set down like that of the men; because there are many in the Church who are either slower in understanding or even carnal, yet devoutly obey their spiritual masters and bend the back of the mind to carry the burdens of their brethren's need, and, rescued with the rest of the elect from the confusion of the devil's captivity, make for the walls of the city above; whose number too is kept entire in the memory of God. Whence: "Thy eyes did see my imperfect being." And elsewhere: "Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord."
18_interl53: going beyond the precepts of the law
18_marg29: BEDE. It is a sign of great devotion to offer to the Lord freely not only the due offerings, that is, those commanded by the law, but also gifts not according to precept but according to counsel. It is commanded by the law: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God, and thy neighbour as thyself", and the rest of this kind. But a voluntary offering is: "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor." As the Apostle [says] of virgins: "I have no commandment of the Lord; but I give counsel." Rightly then the chief of the fathers offer freely for building the house of God; because the more each abstains even from lawful things, the more effectively he builds the Church of God, since those who see the examples of their perfection fear to commit unlawful things all the more, the more they consider that these do not even use lawful things.
18_interl54: this is the measure of human perfection
18_marg30: For this is the measure of perfection, that each should labour for the Lord according to his power, and confirm the state of the Church first in himself, then in his neighbours. Those who so live are rightly called the chief of the fathers, because by living more loftily they have the primacy, in perfection of life and teaching, over those who in the Church are called fathers for their zeal of solicitude.
18_interl56: of polished eloquence: "The words of the Lord are pure words"
18_interl57: works of justice surpassing the manners of the common people and worthy of hearts consecrated to God
18_interl58: "Let thy priests be clothed with justice"
18_marg31: BEDE. The chief of the fathers offer gold and silver and priestly garments, according to their ability, for the expenses of the works of the temple, when holy men, by living well, bestow on the edification of the faithful whatever of wisdom, eloquence and good action they receive. The weight of the gold and silver is fixed, the number of the priestly garments is fixed, that we may know that the Lord knows thoughts and words and deeds and rewards them worthily.
18_marg32: But it is to be noted how much the captivity profited the people of God. For those who, according to Jeremias, four thousand six hundred, were [carried] into captivity, being multiplied among the enemies, returned to their homeland nearly fifty thousand men; and those who had been poor and servants return enriched with gold, silver, garments and servants; and those who lost their homeland because of the multitude of false gods now return home rejoicing in the faith of the one true God, worshipping that very faith with unanimous devotion, so that those who because of the diversity of religion were called by divers names, Juda and Israel, are now for the unity of piety all called by the ancient name Israel. For the worship of piety, which they despised in the holy land while the prophets cried out against them [so the edition: 'reclinantibus'] and showed examples of justice, they now loved in a foreign land, among enemies who served idolatry. For those whom liberty and plenty in their homeland made negligent of the heavenly commandments, servitude and want in exile brought to the obedience of the Creator. For the human body [so the edition] is loosened by riches and liberty, and by hardships and poverty is gathered back to itself. What therefore was done once in that people is wont to be done daily in all penitents, when those who through negligence fell into the snares of the devil rise again, divinely helped, through the diligence of penance; and those who, stripped of the works of the virtues by the devil, departed from the Church return to its communion to be exercised in greater virtues. For the more gravely they remember that they have erred, the more ardently they apply themselves to good works.
18_marg33: The Levite taken captive by the Chaldeans recovers his city when a deacon, by the Lord's gift, restores the virtue of perfection which he had lost when seduced by the devil. But the one born in Babylon, coming into Judea, enters the city when one regenerated in Christ and well instructed in the Church keeps according to rule the diaconate once received. For as the former was freed by the grace of Christ as from the Chaldean bondage, so the latter, by carrying out the good works in which the predecessors of the same grade lived, ascend as it were to the walls of their own virtue or city.
18_marg34: BEDE. By all Israel he means not only the ten tribes, which were once called Israel to distinguish them from the two which were called Juda, but in general all who returned, whether of Juda and Benjamin or of the other tribes. For when the ten tribes had been carried over to the Assyrians and the Samaritans put in their land in their place, whoever had remained left [their land], and broke the idols, and began to serve the Lord with a whole heart and to sacrifice in the temple, as it is written in Paralipomenon. These then who were left were [carried] into captivity with the tribe of Juda and Benjamin, with whom they had been joined, and returned together to their homeland and to their cities, which they found empty with their fields and villages. For no settler had entered them while they themselves served in Babylon, as neither [had any entered] the lands of the two tribes. For the land kept her sabbaths all the days of the desolation. But the greater part of the ten tribes, taken captive by the Assyrians beyond the mountains of the Medes, never returned; nor, if it returned, could it enter its cities, which the Samaritans possessed; of whom the Jews promise themselves that, when their Christ reigns, they will return into Judea with the other men of their nation and will reign in the whole world. Allegorically. The priests, Levites, singers, porters and Nathinites, and all Israel dwell in their cities when the ministers of the altar and the doctors and the Christian people serve God faithfully in their grades, whether those who, the same grade having once been defiled or lost by vices, have been corrected through penance, or those who, coming lately from the kingdom of the devil to the Church, have acquired for themselves a good grade. For the Levites or sons of Israel entered their own cities, not only those who had lost them when taken captive, but also those who, begotten of the captives, had learned that they belonged to them by paternal succession. But whoever were so taken captive that, never returning, they left their estates to others to possess, signify those who by sinning so depart from the Church that they never come to their senses, and leave to others the rewards promised to them. Whence: "Be mindful from whence thou art fallen, and do penance, and do the first works. Or else I come to thee, and will move thy candlestick out of its place" etc. And elsewhere: "Hold fast that which thou hast, that no man take thy crown."
18_marg35: AND NOW THE SEVENTH MONTH WAS COME, which with us is October, solemn above the others by the observance of the law, in which also the dedication of the temple was celebrated. Fittingly therefore, as soon as they had entered their cities and provided dwellings for themselves, they forthwith flocked together to Jerusalem and built the altar, and that at the time at which the temple with the altar and all the vessels had once been consecrated, and at which they were wont to come every year for the day of the consecration.
18_marg36: Mystically. The seventh month signifies the grace of the Holy Spirit. In this month after the captivity we come together from our cities to Jerusalem when, the filth of vices being taken away, after the beginning of good works we are enlightened by the greater grace of the same Spirit and are kindled with love of the peace above, which is in true unity. For Jerusalem is called 'vision of peace'.
18_marg37: Of the priestly tribe, which signifies Christ the true priest, who "hath washed us from our sins in his own blood" and "now appears in the presence of God for us".
18_marg38: AND HIS BRETHREN THE PRIESTS etc. Of whom it is said: "Go, tell my brethren." These are the higher in the Church and, cleaving more familiarly to Christ, build up the Church. To the whole Church too it is said: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood." For the elect are members of the supreme Priest, offering their bodies a living sacrifice.
18_interl61: because without it they do not please
18_interl62: renouncing the world altogether and following Christ
18_interl63: acting manfully and strongly in all things
18_marg39: BEDE. With great foresight they first built the altar, so that, because the temple was not yet founded, they might yet have where, sacrificing, they could show the devotion of their mind. Which we too do spiritually today, when before all things we place in our heart the faith of the Lord's incarnation and passion and hand it on to our hearers; whence: "I judged not myself to know any thing among you, but Jesus Christ, and him crucified." On this altar we offer our holocausts, that is, perfect thoughts and works. For so the vows of our actions please God the Father, if we partake of the sacraments of Christ, if we are kindled by the power of the Holy Spirit as by the fire of the altar. For a holocaust is called 'wholly burnt', by which name those sacrifices were called of which nothing went to human uses, but the whole was given to God and consumed by the highest fire. By these is expressed the life of the faithful, who seek nothing of their own but spend all that they live in the service of God. And they rejoice not only to trample the will of body and soul for the Lord, but to lay down their very soul for him, saying with the apostles: "Behold we have left all things, and have followed thee" etc. To whom it is answered: "Every one that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters" etc. This holocaust is to be offered on the altar of God, because unless in the faith of Christ it cannot be accepted. For many philosophers left their own things and, leading a clean and poor life, seemed to make a holocaust, but they did not do this on the altar of God, because they left pleasures, but "did not have Christ as advocate with the Father".
18_interl64: because opposition of wicked spirits or men at once withstands undertakings devoted to God
18_interl65: not of those whose "conversation is in heaven"
18_marg40: ITS BASES etc. That is, the hearts of the elect, prepared to receive the sacraments of faith by the precepts of the masters, as by the tools of craftsmen. And well is there one altar, but many bases which carry it; because there is "one God, one faith", but many hearts of the faithful, which, instructed by one rule of truth and as it were gathered into an equal bosom, carry with common devotion the burden of the heavenly sacraments. But he who commits the sacraments of faith to the less instructed and to those who do not forsake their vices, as it were sets the altar of the Lord on the earth without bases, because he hands heavenly things to minds still earthly. Whence: "Neither do men light a candle and put it under a bushel, but upon a candlestick" etc. For as Christ is called an altar, because he amends from iniquities and commends the vows of prayers to the Father, so also a candle, because he placed the light of divinity in the earthen vessel of humanity. And the bases are set under the altar and the candlestick under the candle when the faithful with humble intention submit their hearts and bodies to practising by work what they believe.
18_marg41: BEDE. Morning and evening we offer a holocaust to the Lord upon his altar when, faith in him being established in our heart, we give our effort to good acts with entire devotion; and this morning and evening, namely when we remember that we received from him the beginnings of saving intention, and that we do not perfect what we have begun except through the help of his grace. And therefore we offer him vows of thanks in all things with ardent desire of a pious life. Again we make a holocaust in the morning when, for the light of spiritual knowledge received, we render God the return of living well; but in the evening when we burn with unceasing zeal for the everlasting rest which we hope for in him after good works. It can also rightly be taken according to the letter that we offer a holocaust morning and evening when we take care to please God at all times in such a way that, rising at dawn, we do not go forth to do the necessary things of human frailty before, inflamed with the fire of divine charity, we commend ourselves to the Lord with devout prayers; whence: "In the morning my prayer shall prevent thee." Likewise, when the works of the day are finished, let us not give sleep to our eyes before we consecrate a place for the Lord in ourselves by earnestness in prayer, according to that: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight; the lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice."
18_marg42: BEDE. Those who had gone up from Babylon to Jerusalem, burning to fulfil all the commandments of the Lord, desired to celebrate this solemnity on each day of the week which the law had commanded, fulfilling what it befits us to fulfil spiritually. For we went out of Egypt through the blood of the lamb, that we might come to the land of promise, when, baptized with the sacrament of the Lord's passion, we cast off the heavy yoke of transgression, that, adopted "into the liberty of the glory of the children of God", we may be heirs of the heavenly kingdom. And we dwelt in tabernacles, going through the desert a long time until we should come to the homeland, when in baptism, renouncing Satan as the kingdom of Egypt, that is, of darkness, and all the pomps and works of the world, we promised that we were as pilgrims and wayfarers in the world, citizens of another life which we hope for from the Lord. In memory of this hope of promise we ought to dwell in tabernacles in the seventh month, and, the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit enlightening us, all the day long to forsake the world as dry and foreign, and with fixed intention to hasten to the unfading joys of paradise; and this for seven days, that is, through the whole time of the present life, which revolves in so many days. On each day of this week too we ought to make a holocaust, and the work of the day in its day: the offering, namely, wholly burnt, in those things which properly belong to the divine service, as prayers and fasts; and the work of the day in its day in those things which belong to the service of brotherly love, as ministering bread to the hungry, drink to the thirsty, and the like. Paul hinted that these solemnities of tabernacles were to be celebrated by us mystically, when in the midst of preaching he gave himself to the craft of tent-making. For he made tents to teach that he was a pilgrim, and that those whom he instructed were pilgrims in this life but hoped for a homeland in the future; whence: "While we are in the body, we are absent from the Lord"; and elsewhere: "For we have not here a lasting city, but we seek one that is to come."
18_marg43: Which in Greek is called Scenopegia, that is, the pitching of tabernacles, which begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and lasts seven days, in which the Lord commanded the people to dwell in tabernacles and, searching the law daily, to offer holocausts to the Lord; because they once dwelt in tabernacles, namely in the wilderness, while Moses preached the law and God often appeared to them, long awaiting the promised rest; that, namely, the grace of so great a benefit might never come into forgetfulness.
18_marg44: Because whatever is done without order loses the merit of perfection, for "the king's honour loveth judgment". For in what we do for the honour of the supreme King it is necessary that we distinguish with sure discretion of judgment when and how much is to be done.
18_interl67: as it were, namely, apart from the general commandments, we offer freely to God, of which it is said not by commanding but by counselling: "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast" etc. And elsewhere by persuading: "He that can take, let him take it."
18_marg45: That is, at the beginnings of the months at the rising of the moon, from which the Hebrews always began their months, having no months except lunar ones; hence, for calends, the Greeks better call them neomenias, that is, new moons. And if the months, because of the thirty days by which they are filled, signify the fullness of the works of light, when in the faith of the holy Trinity we perfect the precepts of the decalogue, what do the beginnings of the months, in which the moon is said to be newly kindled by the sun that it may shine again, designate, if not the beginnings of good work, which by the gift of the Creator's grace we receive as by the presence of the sun of justice? For the signifying of which divine illumination, without which we can neither begin nor perfect anything good, God commanded all the calends, that is, the beginnings of the months, to be celebrated; whence: "Blow up the trumpet on the new moon, on the noted day of your solemnity." And well is it said that, the feast of tabernacles being ended, the children of the transmigration made the continual holocaust etc.; because after the mind has once perfectly renounced this world, it must spend itself wholly in the service of the divine will.
18_marg46: That is, from the beginning of divine inspiration, by which the human conscience is changed and, pleasures being neglected, burns for those things alone which are the Lord's; like the apostles, who, inflamed by the Holy Spirit and made as it were a holocaust, preached the wonderful works of God in all tongues. Hence among the Hebrews the seventh month is called the new year, because through the Holy Spirit it is given to the faithful to fulfil the new commandment of charity and to render a new song in the building of the house of God.
18_marg47: But it is to be noted that in the seventh month the people was gathered in Jerusalem, and, all being gathered, Josue and Zorobabel with their brethren are related to have built the altar and from the first day of the seventh month to have offered holocaust; from which it is gathered that this altar was very quickly put together of unhewn stones, not, as formerly, wrought of wood and covered with plates of brass. For not otherwise, even with a very great crowd of builders pressing on, could it be begun and finished in one day and prepared for offering holocaust. For in the book of Machabees it is said to have been made of stones: "And they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar according to the former."
18_marg48: It is to be noted that the beginning of the fifth age, like that of the four preceding, is consecrated by holocausts offered to the Lord. For in the first, the protomartyr Abel, first of all the elect, offered God a holocaust of the firstlings of the sheep, and dedicated the entrance of the newborn world first with victims of cattle, at length with his own blood. Noe consecrated the rise of the second age by holocausts offered to God of those things which had been in the ark. Melchisedech and Abraham consecrated the third age, the one with bread and wine, the other by offering his own son. David consecrated the fourth age to the Lord, building an altar in the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite and offering holocausts to God, by which he appeased him whom he had offended by numbering the people; where Abraham is said to have offered his son, and where, after the temple was built by Solomon, the altar of holocausts is known to have been placed. Now Josue and Zorobabel offered the beginning of the fifth age, building an altar in the same place and offering holocausts to God as soon as the yoke of captivity was shaken off, and afterwards appeased the Lord to themselves with the continual holocaust. All these things went before in figure of him who in the sixth age redeemed the whole world with the victim of his flesh.
18_interl69: that they might work more readily
18_marg49: BEDE. Those who, freed from the captivity, came to Jerusalem, purposed to make the temple and afterwards made it; but, the altar first being set up, they commended themselves to the Lord with daily holocausts, that they might deserve to build the temple itself worthily. Let him therefore who wishes to teach others first teach himself, lest he hear from the Apostle: "Thou therefore that teachest another, teachest not thyself." Whence: "I chastise my body, and bring it into subjection: lest perhaps, when I have preached to others" etc. Rightly therefore the children of the transmigration are related to have offered to God no other sacrifices than holocausts, that is, offerings wholly burnt; because he who desires by teaching to restrain those who live ill from unlawful things must give himself over wholly to the Creator by living well and by abstaining even from lawful things.
18_marg50: It can also be said that, the altar being built, they offer holocausts to God but do not yet build the temple, so that they can be numbered among the perfect even if they do not yet receive the time or means of doing or perfecting the good things they desire; as Abraham was already perfect in faith when he had not yet perfected works. Whence: "Abraham believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice." But when he offered his son upon the altar, he rendered to God more perfect holocausts, as it were with the temple built. For the several acts or steps of pious devotion are the courses of polished stones with which we may build in our heart a dwelling beloved of God.
18_marg51: The founding of the temple signifies those who, lately converted, prepare a place for the Lord in themselves; whence: "Your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost" etc.
18_interl71: namely examples of the virtues, or the scriptures, strengthened by which they may not grow weary
18_interl72: to the preachers, the hewers of stones
18_marg52: Mystically. BEDE. The hewers of stones in the building of the house of God are those who instruct the hearts of their neighbours by teaching or rebuking; whom, while they teach them to stand firm among others, they fit as it were by squaring. For whichever way you turn a square it will stand; and the mind of the elect, while it remains unmoved among adversities or prosperities, shows that it has in itself the square figure of virtue. Hence the ark of Noe is described as made of squared timber. For the same Church is figured by the temple made of stone, by the ark framed of timber, and by the tabernacle composed of curtains and boards.
18_interl73: who make mortar to cement the stones. The pious diligence of the people is to be noted: from their own necessaries they either buy materials or hire workmen
18_marg53: MASONS etc. The masons likewise are preachers who, while they bind one to another with the bond of charity those whom they train in good works, join them as squared and polished stones by pouring in mortar, lest they loosen the order of the structure, saying: "But before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves." Hence Paul: "But above all these things have charity, which is the bond of perfection."
18_interl74: Tyre and Sidon, most noble cities of Phenicia, near mount Libanus
18_marg54: Those of Sidon and Tyre also represent the preachers, who with the axe of the word of God cast down men once lofty and splendid in the glory of the world from the state of their former life, that, laid low to their salvation and as it were dried out from the corrupting moisture of their inborn sense, they may correct them from every crookedness of vices and fashion them for the adornment or defence of the Church. Hence in the Psalm which is entitled "At the finishing of the tabernacle": "The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars."
18_marg55: TO THEM OF SIDON AND TYRE etc. The chief of the fathers, namely Josue and Zorobabel and their brethren, give food and oil to those of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar wood from Libanus to the sea of Joppe, when they commend to the doctors, that they may be able to preach, the spiritual gifts which went before in Christ, to be imitated. Or when Christ, who is signified in Josue and Zorobabel, distributes the spiritual gifts of his word, enlightened inwardly by which they are made stronger to overthrow the boasting of the proud [so the edition: 'supernorum'] and foolish wisdom. Whence: "Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me. Thou hast anointed my head with oil." Money therefore is given to the hewers of stones and masons, and food, drink and oil to the cutters of timber, that they may prepare material for building the house of God, when an abundance of the virtues is divinely bestowed on the preachers by grace, helped by which they are sufficient to correct the hearts of the wicked and to fit them for the reception of good things.
18_marg56: To those of Sidon, the hunters, who catch the wandering senses for Christ with the nets of faith. Whence: "I will make you to be fishers of men." The same are 'distressed', because they have distress in the world, though confident that the Lord has overcome the world.
18_marg57: They carry the felled timber into the sea, not to be sunk, but to be carried through it to Joppe, which is interpreted 'beauty', when the doctors foretell to the hearers called to the faith that temptations will meet them but are to be overcome by faith; that first the wild fruits [so the edition: 'feri fructus'] of vices or of wicked men may be taken away, and so one may come to the beautiful walls and the harbour of the virtues; as it were that we may first renounce the devil, namely the dragon, king of all things that are in the waters, that is, of the impious, who live in the sea, that is, in the turmoils of the world, and afterwards come to the beauty of the faith by which we confess the holy Trinity and one Godhead, the dispensation of the incarnation of Christ, the unity of the Church, the remission of sins and the resurrection of the flesh. Hence Peter raised Tabitha in this city, because in the perfection of this faith and of the universal Church we are raised from the death of sins through baptism; and when after baptism we incur the death of sin, through the same we revive by repenting and are joined again to the Church through the reconciliation of the priests.
18_interl75: this is a maritime city about forty miles distant from Jerusalem
18_marg58: From where, that is, they might be carried by land for the work of the temple, as was done in the first building of the temple. But Solomon by royal power easily obtained what he wished from king Hiram; these, however, returning from captivity and not having the power of a kingdom, bought everything.
18_marg59: BEDE. Since it is said above that they came to Jerusalem in the seventh month, but here that in the second year of their coming, in the second month, they began the work of the temple, it is plain that for seven months they prepared stones, mortar, timber and the other necessaries, and began to work at the beginning of the eighth month. For there were six months of the first year and the seventh of the following. Mystically the seventh belongs to the sabbath, in which the Lord, the maker of the world, rested from his works, or Christ rested in the sepulchre after the passion; eight to the first of the sabbath, on which he rose; seven to the hope of our sabbath after death; eight look to the joy of our everlasting blessedness. Since therefore all the working of the elect, who are the house of God, is begun and perfected by the grace of the Spirit, and all is carried out with regard and intention to future rest and immortality, rightly the builders of the temple, holocausts being offered to God from the seventh month, begin to prepare the expenses for the building, and, these being prepared in seven months, they undertake the work in the eighth; nor is any other number set in the preparation of so great a work than that which proclaims the sevenfold grace of the Spirit by which we are helped in working, or the rest of souls or the resurrection of bodies which we hope for in working well.
18_marg60: That is, the place of the temple, where they desired to build the temple. For the Jews are mistaken who say that the walls of the temple were never overthrown by the Chaldeans, but only the roof, since it is plain that Esdras, a child of the transmigration, made the temple from the foundations.
18_marg61: Great was the devotion of the whole people; for they rejoiced that they had returned from captivity, and as much as they abhorred the crimes of the proud city, so much did they desire to see the beauty of Jerusalem; as much as they abominated the shrines, so much did they strive to have the temple of God restored. So not only ought bishops and priests to build up the people of the faithful, that is, the house of God, but the people too, called from the captivity of vices to the vision of true peace, ought to require the ministry of the word from those who know how to speak; which ministers of the word, that is, Levites, are appointed from twenty years and upward, because such are to be appointed and preferred for preaching as not only show the Decalogue to their hearers by doing it, but also keep it undefiled in the sight of God by purity and integrity of heart.
18_marg62: It is not to be doubted that the state of the Church makes progress through the Spirit there where both the bishops, rightly keeping their grade, ordain masters of truth for the people according to rule, and the people itself, by diligently hearing and obeying, compels them not to cease from teaching. But the sloth of our times hurts the greater and the lesser alike, hindering these from preaching the word, those from hearing it, and both from doing it; because we weigh too little how great is the bitterness of the demonic captivity from which we have been rescued, or how great the solemnity to which we are called, of Jerusalem above, the mother of us all, whose pledge we have already received. But let us look upon the excellent works of the fathers, that we may be the more confounded at the faintheartedness of our own mind.
18_marg63: But it is to be noted and very often remembered how much good the evil of the captivity brought; rescued from which, all apply themselves to the heavenly services with an earnestness such as never before. And today too it has profited many who had lived negligently in peace suddenly to have erred and sinned, when, raised up by repenting after the fall, they serve God more watchfully; and those who stood sluggish and idle in innocence, admonished after the ruin that befell them, are girded more skilfully against the snares of the enemy, so that those who had not even offended by caring for their own life, returning, have the care of restoring the temple. But above all the Levites and the sons of Juda, because of the priestly and at the same time royal dignity of the Church, which chiefly build the temple; because all who form the hearts of the faithful by teaching or by living well belong to the body of the true King and Priest, that is, Christ. Hence too the authors of the work were Jesus [Josue], sprung of the priestly tribe, and Zorobabel of the royal tribe.
18_marg64: Not the son of Josedec, that is, but one of the Levites appointed from twenty years and upward to direct the work, of whom were Cedmiel and the sons of Enadab, who together with their sons and brethren took charge of the work enjoined. Above too, in the catalogue of the people, these are mentioned first of the Levites after the priests; from which it is gathered that they were the chiefs of the Levites of that time. Well are the sons of Juda put in the midst of the Levites, giving their effort together to restoring the temple, and because of the same agreement in piety they are said to have acted as one; for this is the order of virtue to be imitated, that all the grades dedicated to God and the common devotion of the people should each for his part build up the Church.
18_marg65: Mystically. When the temple of the Lord has been founded by the masons, the priests stand in their ornaments with trumpets, when, sinners having been converted from error and faith and love of Christ founded in them, the masters of the churches rejoice together and, adorning themselves more diligently with good works, sound with the trumpets of saving doctrine, that by the example of virtues and the persuasion of words they may help the good beginnings of those who have lately come together to the grace of Christ by repenting, or [those who] convert others by teaching. And the Levites stand to praise God with cymbals, when the ministers of the second order serve their Creator with pious acts for the instruction of the neophytes, and this in the sweetness of mutual charity. For cymbals, which touch one another that they may sound, express the works of charity by which the saints stir one another to praise. They praise also by the hand of David the king when they diligently attend to the works of Christ which he did through the flesh, and imitate them as far as they can.
18_marg66: Great devotion of all persons is shown, when, the temple being founded, all praise the mercy of the Lord according to their grade: the priests indeed, adorned with holy vestments as they had been wont while the temple still stood, sounding with trumpets and kindling the heart of the people to the sweetness of the praise above; the Levites singing hymns to the Lord with well-sounding cymbals; the people showing the affection of their heart by praising God with a common shout.
18_marg67: That is, on the instruments which he made, or with the psalms which he instituted, or because David, at the placing of the ark, made Asaph and his brethren chief to give praise to the Lord, as Paralipomenon testifies; of whom again it is said that his sons were under his hand, prophesying by the king. Rightly here, when the sons of Asaph praised and gave glory to the Lord by the hand of David, they are to be understood to have done this according to his ordering.
18_marg68: THEY WEPT, that is, seeing how far the poverty of that time was from the once magnificent power of Solomon, by which the former temple was founded; and they knew that the former temple had been destroyed for their crimes, whose greatness and beauty they could not equal. For what the prophet says: "Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first", does not belong to the greatness or adornment of the house, but to the thing itself; because it was a greater miracle and a more evident power of God that a few remnants of captives finished so great a work, even with enemies resisting, than that a most wealthy king, having no adversary at all, did as he wished with the help of king Cyrus [so the edition], his dearest friend. Again, the glory of the last house [is] greater than of the first, because in the former house the worshippers of the Old Testament preached to the peoples the Scripture of the law and the prophets; in the second, Christ and the apostles proclaim the grace of the New Testament and the entrance of the heavenly kingdom.
18_marg69: They wept. In the building of the spiritual temple weeping and joy together arise in the chiefs. For the doctors rejoice in the salvation of the penitent, but mourn because they ever committed things to be repented of. They themselves who by penance have risen from the death of the soul exult over their salvation; they mourn because they lost it by sinning. The neophytes rejoice that they have been gathered by the grace of the Redeemer; they grieve that with the human race they perished in their first parent, and, the temple of God being as it were corrupted by the enemies, namely the state of immortal body and soul, were removed into Babylon, that is, into the confusion of the present exile. But because, as the progress of the good grows, the envy of the wicked grows, nor are the temptations of the wicked lacking amid the increase of the pious, who strive to hurt the saints either by feignedly showing good or by openly thrusting in evil, it is rightly added: Now [the enemies] heard etc.
18_interl76: the Samaritans, that is, wicked heretics
18_interl79: the peoples who will sit at the right hand
18_interl80: instructing the Church by word or example
18_marg70: BEDE. By the enemies of Juda and Benjamin he means the Samaritans, whom, when the ten tribes had been taken captive, the king of the Assyrians transplanted from divers peoples of the nations into their cities and lands, who afterwards kept in part the law of God which they had received, and no less the idols which they had served before. These, because they abhorred the true worshippers of God, promise help in the work, that, received into fellowship, they might inflict loss. These therefore express false brethren, that is, heretics and wicked catholics, who are enemies of Juda, that is, of confession and praise, which the Church offers through right faith and right and worthy working, and of Benjamin, that is, of the son of the right hand, when they separate those who hear them from the faithful, who are to receive the blessing and the eternal kingdom at the right hand of the Judge. They say therefore: Let us build with you, when heretics seek to have the authority of preaching among catholics given to them, promising that they hold with them the same chastity of right faith and working, that, having received the power of teaching, they may sow cockle in the midst of the good seed, from which Paul received the surname spermologus, that is, 'sower of words'. For they entered the land of the children of Israel not brought in by Josue, not subject to the rule of Jerusalem, but brought into its land by a faithless king, namely by an enemy of the people of God, not to serve the Lord but the adversary of the kingdom. So heretics and false catholics, since they attack the peace of the Church by living perversely [so the edition: 'puer se'] or by teaching, are strangers to the kingdom of Jerusalem and belong rather to the lot of the gentiles, whose idols they serve; and they enter the borders of holy Church not with Jesus Christ as leader but with the devil, whom the king of Assur signifies. So Simon Magus received baptism in the Church not for his own salvation but that he might search out the secrets of the Church more familiarly; which he showed by his end, when he most bitterly attacked as an open enemy the Church which he could not [attack] in the person of a feigned brother.
18_interl81: let us have equal authority of preaching
18_interl82: unclean, namely, because they do not renounce idols; for what concord hath Christ with Belial
18_marg71: It is not for heretics to build the Church, from which they are strangers, but only for those who, cleaving to Christ the true King and Priest, have deserved to be called chief of the fathers, and for the pious care which they have toward those who desire to see Christ.
18_interl83: well is he called the people of the land who tries to trouble the workers of virtue and to hinder the heavenly work
18_marg72: BEDE. How often heretics, not only in cities but also in provinces, by teaching perversely or even by raging, hindered the doctrine of true confession, would that we did not know! For, to say nothing of the master of the gentiles, who, bound for two years in Caesarea because of the persecution of the Jews, held back his tongue from building the house of God, through the snares of heretics Athanasius was a fugitive for many years, Ambrose was besieged in his own city, Hilary was banished into exile, Eusebius suffered martyrdom, many bishops in Africa with their tongues cut out were cast out of their province, others were harassed with divers punishments or slain; and they left the house of God which they had built to be profaned by the peoples of the land, that is, by men seeking their own things, "not the things that are Jesus Christ's", until at a time divinely foreseen the means should be available to wise architects for rebuilding the same house after the captivity.
18_marg73: By the people of Juda, that is, confessing and glorifying, he means him who with an entire mind seeks to build for the Lord, that is, to turn the minds and mouths of all whom he can to doing his will and seeking his glory.
18_marg74: BEDE. The distinction of the words is to be noted, because he says that counsellors were hired for a price against the workers of the temple to defeat their purpose; but neither was the purpose defeated nor the work interrupted until the letter of accusation was written to Artaxerxes, and at his command they hindered them by arm and strength. For then the work was interrupted, and it was not done until the second year of Darius king of the Persians. From which it is gathered that through the whole time of Cyrus, the work having been begun, they pressed on, though more slowly than was right; but when he was dead they were driven from the work, not hindered by wicked counsels but by open attack. For while Cyrus lived, who had commanded the work to be done, the enemies did not dare to oppose his edicts by open struggle, though they did so secretly by suggesting or counselling.
18_marg75: Mystically, heretics, according to the opportunity of the time, now pursue [the Church] in the counsels of malignant doctrines, now with the sharper fight of swords, and sometimes do not fear to harass it with the support of gentile princes. They hinder the hands of the people of Juda when they hold back the Church in its weaker members from the works of pious profession; they strive to defeat the purpose of working when they labour to call minds back even from the intention of good action [so the edition: 'bone ac omnis']. They accuse them before kings when they gain the protection of earthly princes against the Church; how much this harms the faith became known clearer than light in the time of the Arian faithlessness.
18_marg76: BEDE. This Artaxerxes, who, receiving the letter of accusation from the Samaritans, came to Jerusalem and builds [so the edition] the temple, Josephus thinks to be Cambyses the son of Cyrus, who, after his father had held the empire thirty years, reigned eight years; and after him the Magi, reigning one year, had Darius the son of Hystaspes as successor of the kingdom; in whose second year, in which he permitted the temple to be built, the angel, interceding for the people, said in Zacharias: "O Lord of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, and on the cities of Juda, with which thou hast been angry? This is now the seventieth year" etc. But of Assuerus, to whom likewise the letter of accusation is said to have been sent, it is perhaps passed over in silence whether he wrote back or answered anything because, dying in the same year in which he began to reign, he left the height of rule to Artaxerxes, and to him the care of these things; or he was contemporary with Artaxerxes but, as being of lesser power, permitted him to handle and decide these things.
18_marg77: Artaxerxes, who is persuaded and, persuaded, commands that Jerusalem be not built, signifies any gentile prince who is an enemy and persecutor of the Church, or the devil, the adversary of all good men. The Jews who are accused before the king [are] churchmen; the Samaritans who accuse [are] heretics. Hence with a voice fitting to themselves they call Jerusalem a rebellious and most wicked city; for such they judge the catholic unity which they attack. But in truth it is rebellious, and builds the walls and partitions of right faith with the stones of the heavenly testimonies against the darts of the attackers; of which Isaias says: "And salvation shall possess thy walls, and praise thy gates." But it is not to be called most wicked except by those who are wholly turned away from the best choice of their own judgment. Among which it is to be noted that the people of God began to be reckoned by the name of Jews at that time when those were chiefly of the tribe of Juda who, going up from captivity, restored the walls of the city of Jerusalem and the temple, and, the enemies who held the neighbouring places being overcome, again possessed the province emptied of inhabitants.
18_interl84: the Samaritans eat salt in the palace when heretics are trained in the savour of worldly wisdom and philosophy, with the sweetness of rhetoric and the craft of dialectic
18_interl85: the devil or any prince hostile to Christians
18_marg78: Because they cannot bear it if any try to attack the kingdom of the devil; they fear that wars be raised in the Church, lest their heresies and deceits be overthrown together with the doctrine of the gentiles, under that leader who said: "I came not to send peace, but the sword." And again: "I am come to cast fire on the earth" etc.; the sword, namely, of the word of God, with which he lays low the adversaries, the fire of charity, with which, kindling the hearts of his own, he burns all the arms and shields of the contrary sect.
18_interl86: the Church, the city of the great King
18_marg79: THAT THIS CITY etc. The enemies themselves again confess of the city of the Lord that, if it be built after the captivity and its walls of living stones, that is, of holy souls, be raised against the pride of the world, its citizens, that is, the elect, will no longer pay the tribute of wicked servitude to the malignant spirits by sinning; nay, the building of piety will harm the princes of darkness, because daily through the laver of regeneration many are taken from the kingdom of the devil who are begotten corrupted by original sin into his service; who pay the tribute of servitude not undue to the enemy but commanded to the Creator, and render the yearly revenues of their firstfruits and tithes, that is, the beginning and the perfection of good things, to God, from whom they had received them, by living well and giving thanks.
18_interl87: to heretics, namely, and enemies of the truth
18_interl88: I came not to send peace, but the sword
18_interl89: by the persecution of heretics and gentiles
18_marg80: BEYOND THE RIVER etc. That is, the Euphrates, within which is Syria; which signifies baptism, because it is one of the four rivers of paradise which water the whole world, as the four evangelists, inspired from one fountain of life, that is, Christ, with harmonious voice preach the laver of salvation to all nations; or because Euphrates is interpreted 'fruitful', which fits the sacrament by which the world, washed and sanctified, brings forth to God fruit of souls thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold.
18_marg81: The king of the Persians, which is interpreted 'tempting', seeks the possession beyond the river when the ancient enemy, stirring up the assaults of temptations, tries to break into the borders of the Church and to subjugate those who have been redeemed by the sacred font. The Samaritans help him when heretics, attacking the Church, fight for the kingdom of the devil, and say grieving that, if the city be built and the walls repaired, namely through faith and right working, he will have no possession beyond the river, that is, in the hearts of those who have been baptized. For even those who do not understand the right faith understand that light and darkness, iniquity and justice, Christ and Belial, cannot possess the same mind together.
18_marg82: The sense of the letter and of the allegory is plain: that the profane one, that is, the ancient enemy, most willingly favours those who persecute the Church and forbid it to be built.
18_marg83: The enemies of Jerusalem dwell in Samaria, which is interpreted 'keeping', not because those who obstinately resist the vision of true peace keep the precepts of faith and truth, but because they boast that the keeping of the virtues remains with them, while they fight through heresy against the walls of peace.
18_marg84: BEDE. The order of the history is plain: that the enemies of the people of God first hindered the work by pursuing [it], then tried to scatter the purpose of their right intention by wicked counsels; nor were they at all able to draw them back from the work before, propped by royal help, they resisted with public authority. Their fraudulence in accusing is to be noted, by which they complained that those who were building the house of God were building a city against the kingdom; and, when the king commanded that the city be not built, at once seizing the authority, they opposed the building of the temple, though they had reported nothing about the construction of the temple and the king had only forbidden the city to be built.
18_marg85: BEDE. In their books it is written more fully with what words they rebuked the sloth of those who were more negligent toward the work of the temple, or kindled them to work by the promised help of God, and with what devotion too, at their exhortation, Zorobabel, Josue and all the people girded themselves to work. For Aggeus begins thus: "In the second year of Darius the king, on the first day of the aforesaid month, the word of the Lord came by the hand of Aggeus the prophet, saying: Speak to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and to Jesus the son of Josedec" etc. And a little after: "And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, the governor of Juda, and the spirit of Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people: and they went in, and did the work in the house of the Lord" etc. And Zacharias begins thus: "In the eighth month, in the second year of king Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zacharias the son of Barachias, the son of Addo the prophet" etc. From which it appears why Esdras names Zacharias the son of Addo: namely because he was the grandson of him who is understood to have been a noble prophet, whose son Zacharias, excellent among the prophets, would rightly be called. Among which it is to be noted of how great spirit these prophets were, that against the edict of so great a king, and with the Samaritans and all the nations round about hindering the building of the temple, they commanded the temple to be built. Zorobabel too and Jesus [Josue] and the people who were with them are shown to have been of no less faith, who listened to the prophets commanding rather than to the command of the king forbidding.
18_marg86: 'Born in Babylon', or 'master of Babylon', because, according to the history, he was born there, though he was of the stock of David, who was born in Bethlehem. He signifies Christ, who, to free the world from the confusion of errors, deigned to be born and to live in Babylon, that is, in the confusion of the world. Who is also rightly called 'master of Babylon', not because he teaches the things which are of Babylon, that is, of the world, but because those whom he finds pressed by the Babylonian yoke he instructs to the grace of liberty, and, instructed, leads them to the heavenly homeland; whose father is Salathiel, that is, 'my petition, God', who says, namely in the Psalm: "Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance" etc. Each one too, when, calling upon God, he seeks nothing else but him, can call him Salathiel.
18_marg87: BEDE. Josue or Jesus is interpreted 'saviour', Josedec 'the Lord just'. He indeed, like the son of Nun, signifies Christ. For each brought the people into the land of promise, the one from the long sojourning of the wilderness, the other from the longer servitude of the captivity. So the true Jesus, rescuing his elect from all evils, brings them into the promised joys of the kingdom above; who is the son of Josedec, that is, of 'the Lord just', of whom it is said: "The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners" etc.
18_marg88: BEDE. The text of the letter is plain: that, strengthened by the words of the prophets, the nobles of the Jews could not be hindered by the attacks of the enemies from the holy work, from which, while the prophets were still silent, they had ceased through fear of the enemies; as is now done in the Church, when those who, held back by the snares of malignant spirits or men, were at times slower to good work, suddenly rebuked by the words of the doctors or of the divine Scriptures, can be overcome by no engines of temptations nor called back from the purpose of their intention.
18_marg89: He who wrote this seems to have been present, though Esdras is said to have written it, who is found not to have been in Jerusalem at that time, but to have come there long after, in the reign of Artaxerxes. Either therefore he truly was there then, and when the temple was made returned to Babylonia to bring back more of the children of Israel to Jerusalem; or he joins himself to the builders as if what is done toward his brethren, or what they themselves do, were his own; as the Apostle says: "We who are alive, who remain unto the coming of the Lord, shall not prevent them who have slept."
18_marg90: This letter is very unlike that which Reum Beelteem and Samsai wrote to Artaxerxes. For that one is full of accusation of the people of Jerusalem, this one of praise not only of the nation but also of almighty God. That one was written with snares, this one with friendly letters; because that one [was] from the Samaritans, enemies of the Jews, this one from the governor of the region beyond the river, that is, of lower Syria and Phenicia, and from his companions, who had no domestic enmities against the Jews but only took care to carry out the will of the king from whom they had received their power.
18_marg91: The Samaritans, who, writing the first letter, kindled the mind of the king against the builders of the temple, are compared to heretics, who so stain the Church with foul pestilence that they even make it hateful to the gentiles and stir up their fury against it. But the governor of Syria, who does not urge the king to stop the work of God but asks him by consulting, signifies those who, still placed in heathenism, do not refuse to believe if they understand that this Scripture of the Godhead is true and just. Finally, hearing from the ancients of the Jews when they gave their reasons, We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, building etc., he would not hinder them, but with a simple mind asked whether Cyrus had commanded the temple to be built and whether Darius wished it. And, the will of both kings being known, he diligently helped that the work might be finished more quickly.
