All which things fit those who, set in the gentile life, on seeing the life of the Church are suddenly astonished, then are eager to hear and learn the reason of religion, and at length, knowing that it took its origin from the God of heaven and earth, who alone is truly God, share in his sacrifices and rejoice to help the building.
18_marg92: WITH UNPOLISHED STONE, that is, new, which they found unpolished but by polishing fitted to the building. For although of the old stones, which, according to Jeremias, "were scattered at the top of every street", some stones remained, new ones were to be polished with which the work of the temple could be completed. Which we see mystically done in the Church, when it is built not only of those who come to their senses by repenting, but also of those who, lately called to the faith, are framed by the instruction of the masters as by the rule of the craftsmen and placed in the building in fitting order. Of old and new stones too, that is, those long since set and those unpolished, the temple is built, when of both peoples, namely Jew and gentile, the one Church of Christ is gathered. For the one had long since been as it were polished by the knowledge and observance of the law; the other, bound over to idolatry, had put off the deformity of a rustic and earthly mind by no diligence of spiritual architects, by no worship of piety.
18_marg93: BEDE. The timbers which are set for the adornment or defence of the temple designate the same life of the saints in the adornment of the Church as the stones also do; of which it is said: "Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice" etc.
18_marg94: THEN DARIUS etc. BEDE. Josephus has set down the name of the place in which these letters of Cyrus were found thus: And the book was found in Egbathana, a city built in the region of Media. Again, another translation has it thus: In Egbathana, in the safest building of the region of the Medes. Hence it seems that the name Medena signifies nothing other than Media.
18_marg95: BEDE. It is not for us to expound, because neither in the former building of the temple nor in the later is anything found of these measures or of work of this kind; from which it is gathered that Cyrus put this forth from his own mind, and noted the measure or order of the time as seemed fitting to him. For the temple, as Paralipomenon relates, had in its first measure, that is, within the inner walls, sixty cubits of length, twenty of breadth; and of height, as the history of Kings writes, thirty cubits up to the upper chamber, then another thirty up to the higher upper chamber, as far as the height of the porches rose, as Josephus testifies, then sixty up to the top of the roof, that is, a hundred and twenty together, as Paralipomenon teaches. But how does he say that three rows of unpolished stones are to be laid, and so of new timber, when the whole temple was clothed with cedar within? Unless perhaps it was the custom of the Persians to make temples so with varied work, that there should be only rows of stones through the walls, and a fourth of wrought timber; and he thought that this ought to be done also in the temple of the Jerusalemites. Or perhaps it is to be understood that he spoke of the court of the priests, which, made round about the temple, had had three rows of polished stones and a fourth of cedar timber, and was as high as the breast of those standing by. Or of the porch of the house of the Lord, which was before the face of the temple, of which Scripture, when the palace of Solomon was being built, makes mention thus: "And he made the greater court round with three rows of hewn stones, and one row of planed cedar: and also in the inner court of the house of the Lord, and in the porch of the house."
18_interl93: the Babylonian [temple], that is, in which Nabuchodonosor had placed them
18_marg96: Darius confirms the letters with his authority, restraining all the adversaries of the Jews, and commands the temple to be built in its place etc.
18_marg97: Artaxerxes, who forbids the house of God and the city to be built, signifies those who oppose the construction of holy Church by stirring up persecutions, amid which the Church flourished most of all with the victory of the martyrs. But Darius [signifies] the pious devotion of those kings who, having acknowledged the piety of the Christian faith, took care not to resist it but to help it by their decrees; of whom many, forbidding the persecutions of their predecessors, wished themselves with their subject peoples to be consecrated with the sacraments of the same faith; to whom what Darius adds fits well: I have also commanded what must etc. For who could unfold how much the Church has been helped and enriched by the liberality of kings?
18_marg98: THAT OF THE CHEST etc. BEDE. The charges for the work of God are given from the king's chest when, from the household of worldly princes, some come to the faith of Christ with their favour, who were as it were in the king's chest, since they were privy to the royal secrets. But they are given to the priests and ancients of the Jews for the charges of the work of the temple when they are committed to the masters to be united to the members. Such was Cassiodorus, once a senator, suddenly a doctor of the Church; who, while in his exposition of the psalms he diligently attends to what Ambrose, what Hilary, what Augustine, what Cyril, what John, what the other saints said, proved himself taught by the ancients of the Jews, that is, of those confessing and praising God.
18_marg99: BEDE. These animals, which are clean, and the wheat and salt and wine and oil, which were offered according to the law, are often put in signification of good things, either of perfect works or of spiritual gifts; which are now, at the king's command, offered in holocaust to the God of heaven, when, with the princes of the world favouring, the affairs of holy Church grow, and the peoples subject to them are gathered into the one faith of truth to be consecrated to Christ, and whatever natural good each has had from God, whatever wholesome thing he has learned from the men of the Church, he spends wholly on the divine worship.
18_marg100: Because the vows of those who offer will be accepted only when they are offered according to the custom of the catholic peace; but those that are mixed with gentile superstition or heresy are not good.
18_marg101: AND PRAY etc. According to that of the Apostle: "I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men: for kings, and for all that are in high station."
18_marg102: He willed to punish with the most grievous penalty him who should change the decree, namely by the loss of all that he had and of his life, which, fastened also to a beam, he would lose by long torment. Mystically, our works are compared to timbers, the good to fruitful ones, the wicked to willows and to those worthy of burning; and a beam is taken from the house of him who opposes the holocausts of the Lord, and is set up, and he himself is fastened on it, when the works of those who fight against the peace of the Church are made manifest to all, how useless and perverse they are, and they themselves are shown to have gained in them not the joy of life but the snare of death. The house of such men is also confiscated, that is, proscribed by public assessment, when their bodies, with which they lived in this life, are handed over in the resurrection to be punished with perpetual torment into the power of cruel exactors, the unclean spirits.
18_marg103: He desires his decree to be confirmed by the divine power, and he himself, as a man endowed with a temporal kingdom, does by public law all that he can for the peace of the house of God. Which is now also done in the Church, when earthly powers converted to the faith set forth public edicts for the state of the Church, and desire [so the edition: 'capiunt'] always to have this peace calm, with the Lord helping and overthrowing the enemies.
18_marg104: Now too, as the peoples flock to the faith, and sometimes with those who are outside favouring, the ancients of the Jews, that is, those who are worthy of the office of master, build up the Church daily by word and example, and prosper; because even if the devil attacks, the word of God yet finds those in whom it may conquer and, the adversaries being put to flight, may raise the walls of truth.
18_marg105: ACCORDING TO THE PROPHECY etc. For they had foretold that, if they pressed on with building the temple, soon, by the Lord's gift, they would both finish the work itself and abound in all good things.
18_marg106: Let no one think that what Aggeus says, that the foundations of the temple were laid under king Darius, is contrary to this history, in which it is written that in the second year of king Cyrus the temple was founded by the masons, while the people praised God much and rejoiced together. For then the founding of the temple itself was described, that is, of the inner house, whose measures the history of Kings and Paralipomenon specially relates. But now, with the building of the house, those buildings are said to be founded, namely the porches and treasuries which surrounded the house on every side, of which mention is made thus in Paralipomenon: "He made also the court of the priests, and a great hall, and doors in the hall, which he covered with brass." In which hall, namely, set round the temple, the people stood to pray, and the keepers and porters of the temple kept watch [so the edition: 'exultabant'] by turns day and night, as Paralipomenon teaches. These are sometimes numbered generally with the temple itself, as in the gospel, where, while he was teaching in the temple, the Pharisees and scribes brought the woman taken in adultery, whom they could in no way have brought in except into some porch of the temple. Sometimes they are separated under the name of treasuries, or of exedra, or of porches, or of courts. Whence: "You that stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God."
18_interl94: who reigned after Darius, in whose time Esdras went up from Babylonia to Jerusalem
18_marg107: It is asked how the house is said to have been built by the command of Artaxerxes, since it is at once added that it was completed and dedicated while Darius still reigned; unless perhaps it is to be believed that Artaxerxes too, sending gold and silver, commanded that whatever was less completed in the building or adornment of the temple or of the vessels should be perfected. For when Esdras was hastening there it is written that the same king with his princes or counsellors sent very much gold and silver and vessels to the temple.
18_marg108: BEDE. On whose third day the house was completed. It is March, which Scripture is wont to call the twelfth according to the course of the moon. Nor is it without mystery that the house of the Lord, which was begun in the seventh month with the building of the altar, was perfected in the twelfth month. For it was begun at the beginning of the seventh month, because every good thing that we do we begin with the preventing grace of the Holy Spirit and perfect with the same accompanying. And it was completed in the twelfth month for the signifying of perfection, which is contained in this number, chiefly because of the sum of the apostles, in whose faith and teaching the Church is perfected. Again, the number twelve signifies the perfection of faith and working, because whether you multiply three by four or four by three you will make twelve. And three are referred to faith because of the confession of the holy Trinity, four to good work because of the four principal virtues, prudence, fortitude, temperance and justice, of which it is said: "For she teacheth temperance, and prudence, and justice, and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in life." Rightly therefore the house of the Lord, begun in the seventh month, was perfected and dedicated in the twelfth, because the mind of the elect is enlightened by the grace of the Holy Spirit that it may come to the perfection of good working with the faith of the holy Trinity, and so, rejoicing, awaits the dedication of the reward. And since this reward of the future solemnity is perfected in the time of the universal resurrection and in the vision of the Trinity, rightly the house of the Lord is recorded as completed not only in the twelfth month [but] on its third day; for because the Lord rose on the third day, our resurrection can be signified by the number three, of which it is said: "On the third day he will raise us up." And the building of the temple was begun in the first year of king Cyrus and finished in the sixth year of Darius, which are, according to the chronicle, forty-five years. For Cyrus reigned thirty years; after him Cambyses his son eight, who in this volume, as Josephus holds, is called Artaxerxes; after him the Magi, who killed him, one year; after them Darius, up to the finishing and dedication of the temple, six years; which are forty-five years. But it is asked how the Jews answered: "Six and forty years was this temple in building" etc. But if we read the history of Josephus, which adds three years after the finishing and dedication of the temple, in which the peribolus, that is, the construction of fortifications set round the temple, and certain other things which remained, were perfected, we shall see that the sum of forty-six years could rightly be reckoned in the building of the temple, in which all the more eminent things were completed.
18_marg109: But the temple, although it signifies the elect soul because of the Spirit of Christ dwelling in it, and the whole Church, that is, the congregation of all the elect angels and men, also expresses the very body of Christ, born of the virgin, living in the world without sin, loosed by death and raised on the third day; to which is specially fitted that it is said to have been built in forty-six years. For the natural philosophers say that in this number of days the human body grows in the womb from the time of conception to the perfect outlines of the members. And it was fitting that the house which signified the Lord's body [should be built] in that number of years in Jerusalem, that is, [which] is called the city of the great king and the vision of that peace of which it is said: "For he is our peace, who hath made both one." As also that: "The door for the middle side was on the right hand of the house: and by winding stairs they went up to the middle chamber, and from the middle to the third", specially figured the body of Christ, of which it is said: "One of the soldiers with a spear opened his side" etc. For the door of the middle side was on the right-hand part of the house, that is, beginning from the eastern corner of the southern side and leading little by little by a hidden way through the inner parts of the same side to the higher chambers; because Christ willed the door of salvation to be opened to us in his right side, washed and sanctified by whose sacred things we may enter into the higher hall of the heavenly kingdom. For we ascend through the door of the middle side into the upper chamber when, consecrated by the water of baptism and the draught of the Lord's chalice, we pass from this earthly consecration to the life of the heavenly souls. And from the upper we pass into the third when we crown the blessedness of souls with the receiving also of immortal bodies.
18_marg110: Rightly do the children of the transmigration rejoice, who escaped the captivity and deserved to build the house of God, and as devout servants of God offer victims at the dedication of his house, and as lovers of the brotherhood [offer] for the sin of all Israel, wherever they were, asking God to be propitious to them and either to keep them among the enemies or to call them back to the homeland. And rightly is the temple dedicated with joy by the priests and Levites and the rest of the children of the transmigration, because when sinners are corrected there is joy in heaven before the angels of God, and [to] the masters who laboured for their salvation, and [to] all who [unclear in the edition: "de re transmigrarunt"]. The priests therefore and Levites and all the people rejoice at the dedication of the restored house, because all the orders of the Church rejoice over sinners reconciled through penance.
18_marg111: They offer victims at the dedication when they give thanks to God for the conversion of those who strayed, when many, seeing their devotion, gird themselves to greater works of the virtues, lest they be slower in working than those than whom they were more innocent by sinning less. Many too who went before in the faith emulate the more fervent zeal of the novices.
18_marg112: He-goats are offered in this life for sin when the elect beseech God that they may be freed from sins; they are offered in the future when those who have been freed give thanks. And therefore they will sing the mercies of the Lord for ever, because they will always remember that they were wretched and were freed by his gift.
18_marg113: They offer also for the sin of all Israel, because it behoves us so to favour the good who are with us, so to make their good things ours by imitating them, that we pray the Lord also for the state of the whole Church. Hence in the Lord's prayer no one asks anything specially for himself, but for all who have the same Father in heaven. Again, when the temple is built the dedication follows, when, the sum of the elect being completed at the end of the world, it will come to the grace of the heavenly rewards, in which victims are offered, of which the same house, that is, the Church, rebuilt through the glory of immortality after the captivity of mortal hardship, says: "Thou hast broken my bonds, O Lord: I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise." And because they are offered not only for the gifts of the virtues but also for the worldly filth of vices, well, after the calves, rams and lambs, are he-goats offered for the sin of all Israel; for the grace by which he confers the benefits of the virtues also takes away crimes. Nor has Pelagius a place in the house of God, who persuaded himself and his followers that by freedom of will they could either be freed from evils or be confirmed in good things.
18_marg114: Order required that, the house of God being built, priests and Levites should at once be ordained to minister in it. Which is to be observed by those who build monasteries magnificently, that they establish in them doctors who may exhort the people to the works of God, not serve their own pleasures there.
18_marg115: BEDE. When he says that the priests were set in their orders and the Levites in their courses, he signifies the courses of the weeks, in which the whole company of each grade was distributed into twenty-four parts, so that each order in the turn of its week ministered in the temple for eight days, namely from sabbath to sabbath, and after twenty-four weeks, free from the offices of the temple, took care of its own affairs, as Paralipomenon relates. For they had already made the porches of the temple round about the inner sanctuary, at whose doors the Levites kept watch by turns, as is said there. But what he says, As it is written in the book of Moses, belongs not to the courses of the Levites but to the works of God. For Moses wrote what the priests, what the Levites should do in the house of God; but the courses of the Levites and the orders of the priests by twenty-four lots were described not by Moses but by king David with the prophets, priests and Levites of his time. And now too, the Church being built and dedicated through the regeneration of peoples new in the faith, it is fitting that priests and Levites be set in their orders and in their courses, who are over the works of God, that the peoples may not only rest on the sacraments of the faith, but may be girded by the examples and instruction of the just who went before to do the things that are God's; and this not according to the reach of human wit, but as it is written in the book of Moses; with which agrees that of the gospel: "Going therefore, teach ye all nations; baptizing them etc., teaching them to observe all the commandments of God." For we ought to teach our hearers not our own things but the commandments of the law and the gospel, if we take care to come together with them to the rewards of the Lord.
18_marg116: Therefore, the house of the Lord being built and dedicated, the celebration of the Pasch is specially recorded, though no one doubted that men so religious celebrated the Pasch at its time, that it might be mystically hinted that this is the summit of perfection, when, all the allurements of the world being passed by, we always meditate with the whole intention of the mind on the entrance into the other life. For Pasch is interpreted 'passing', because in it the children of Israel, through the immolation of the lamb, passed from Egyptian bondage to liberty; or the lamb itself, that is, Christ, immolated for us, passed out of this world to the Father; which we imitate when we pass from the lowest pleasures to seeking heavenly things, and truly perfect when, loosed from the prison of the flesh, we enter the heavenly kingdom.
18_marg117: Why is the Pasch related after the house was built, when it was said before that from the first day of their coming to Jerusalem they offered lawful victims and holocausts on all the solemnities of the Lord, unless that it might be hinted that they completed the building of the temple with the same devotion of mind with which they began? For there it was said before that the people was gathered as one man, and Josue and his brethren rose up and built the altar to sacrifice holocausts on it. And now, the temple being dedicated as the forty-sixth year was at hand, the same piety of religion is recorded to have been in the minds of all, when it is said that the priests and Levites had been purified, all as one clean for sacrificing the Pasch. For what greater perfection can there be in this life than the unity of a clean multitude? For there were many thousands of priests, many of Levites, but all purified and clean to celebrate the Pasch "with one heart and one soul". Nor was the unity in the people unequal, when it is said: to sacrifice the Pasch for all the children of the transmigration and for their brethren the priests and for themselves; and at once it is added: And the children of Israel did eat etc. For all therefore the Pasch was sacrificed, all did eat, not only those who had returned from the captivity but also all who, settled anywhere before, separated themselves to them at that time. Which can be understood also of the proselytes, who, gentiles by nature, were converted to their rite by circumcision and purified with victims, that they might be worthy of participation in the saving sacrament. Nowhere else, unless I am mistaken, since they went out of Egypt, are they found to have been of such devotion together with the priests and Levites, namely their masters. But this devotion was made [so the edition: 'sacra'] by divine chastisement, because, handed over to enemies for their sins, but freed by penance and confession, they were to serve God better. We see also those who profaned the temple of their body by sinning, and through this were taken captive by the devil, return through penance, by which they might repair a dwelling for the Lord in themselves. For it is to be noted that Solomon finished the former temple in the greatest peace of the kingdom, in a short time and with no one opposing; but the children of the transmigration restored it, when destroyed for their sins, with great compunction of heart, persisting in long labour and often hindered by enemies, at length divinely helped. For it is easy for any convert to renounce the devil, to confess the one and true God, and to receive the sacraments of Christ, and, initiated by these in the remission of all sins, to be made his temple, and to keep the innocence of life received with his grace accompanying. But it is of much labour, if anyone despises by sinning the sacraments of faith received, to recover his former dignity; because he cannot be baptized again, but the sin must be washed away by the long labour of penance; to whose washing the very habit of vices, like the hostile crowd of the Samaritans, resists, the harder to overcome the longer it has possessed the land of the heart empty of virtue.
18_interl97: there are also nations of heaven, who, namely, separated from these, serve the Lord in unity and chastity and celebrate his solemnities with a sincere heart
18_interl98: "With the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth"
18_marg118: BEDE. In this place the celebration of the Pasch can be referred to the resurrection, so that the building of the temple signifies the present state of the Church, the dedication the future life, which is passed in the joy of souls when they have gone out of the body; the immolation of the Pasch the glory of the resurrection, when the spotless elect are refreshed with the flesh of the lamb, not believing in the sacrament but in the thing itself and in truth. Hence here all are said to have been present at the Pasch as one, because then truly [shall be seen] "the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sins of the world". Whence John: "The blood of Jesus the Son of God cleanseth us from all sin." Then will there be true unity, when "God shall be all in all", and the solemnity of unleavened bread in joy, when, no leaven of malice and wickedness remaining, all will cleave to the divine vision in truth and sincerity of heart, not for the seven days of the passing world but for the one day of everlasting life in the courts of the Lord, which is better above [thousands]. [unclear in the edition: "ratione tanti operis ponitur numerus, quam ille cui septiformem gratiam spiritus qua operantes adiuvamur, et requiem animarum aut resurrectionem corporum quam bene operantes speramus denuntiat"]
18_marg119: Because through all the time of the world life is to be led in sincerity and truth, nay in the victims and holocausts of all good things; because Christ at the paschal time tasted death in passing, but conquered it by the eternal power of the resurrection.
18_marg120: WITH JOY etc. For this is the greatest joy of the just now and in the future: that the work of justice, or of the Church, has been perfected, the gentiles too being converted who once resisted, and [turned] to helping its state, that is, to confirming the peace of the Christian religion throughout the world.
18_marg121: BEDE. Up to this point are described, under Zorobabel and Josue, the return of the people from Babylon to Jerusalem, the bringing back of the vessels, the dedication of the temple, the celebration of the solemnities, and the dedication of the canticles of the Lord, which could not be sung in a strange land; all which contain the pattern of human salvation in Christ, when those who had come into the world with original sin are saved, purified by the sacraments of faith, or those who corrupt the faith by sinning come to their senses by repenting, and both, through the same Saviour, the true King and true Priest, celebrating the Pasch, pass from the world to the Father, from death to life. But because, when the temple was burnt and the city overthrown, the Scriptures too were burnt up, and it was necessary by the Lord's mercy that these be repaired, so that those who had restored the overthrown buildings might have that by which, admonished, they themselves might learn to be restored within, there well follows: After these things etc.
18_marg122: BEDE. This Artaxerxes, under whom Esdras went up from Babylonia to Jerusalem, Josephus thinks to be Xerxes the son of Darius, who reigned after him; but the books of chronicles [make him] the successor of that same Xerxes. For Darius, under whom the temple was built, reigned thirty-six years; after him Xerxes twenty years; after him Archabanus seven months, which the chroniclers set down as a year; after him Artaxerxes forty years.
18_interl99: the generation being reckoned up to Aaron, he was reckoned a lawful priest
18_marg123: AND HE WAS A READY SCRIBE. BEDE. Esdras is called a ready scribe in the law of Moses because Esdras restored the law of Moses, which had been consumed; and also, as is the common report of our elders, he wrote the whole series of sacred Scripture which the fire had consumed, as seemed sufficient to readers, and, as they relate, added some things which he thought fitting; of which is that: "And there arose no more a prophet in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face" etc. Which words no one could have said except one who lived long after Moses. And in the book of Samuel: "In time past in Israel, when a man went to consult God, he spoke thus: Come, let us go to the seer. For he that is now called a prophet, in time past was called a seer." And some whole volumes which were once had among the people of Israel, as is that in the book of Numbers: "Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord", and in Josue: "Is not this written in the book of the just?" In the volume of Kings and Paralipomenon too are mentioned historical books of the prophets Ahias the Silonite, and Semeias, Addo, and Nathan; of Isaias too, and of Jehu the son of Hanani, who is said to have written the book of the Kings of Israel; and many others, of which no traces can be found today. The Hebrews also relate for certain that he devised lighter letters under the names of those which they had had before, with which he might most quickly restore so great an abundance of books which had been consumed. Therefore he is named not only scribe but also ready. But the former letters remained with the Samaritans, with which they were wont to write those five books of Moses, which alone of holy Scripture they had received.
18_interl100: prolepsis. For in what follows it is written more fully how they came and gathered a host
18_marg124: BEDE. It is to be noted that at the head of this book it is written that, by the permission of Cyrus, Zorobabel and Josue went up from Babylon, and of the children of Juda and Benjamin with the priests and Levites all whose spirit God had raised up; of whom it was added that they were of the captivity which Nabuchodonosor carried away into Babylon. But here, under Esdras as leader, there is no mention of Juda and Benjamin or of Nabuchodonosor, but only of the children of Israel and of the priests and Levites who went up with him. Hence it seems that those were of Juda and Benjamin whom Nabuchodonosor took captive; but these of the ten tribes, which after the division were specially called Israel, whom the kings of the Assyrians had taken captive long before and had made to dwell beyond the mountains of the Medes. Then therefore the two tribes for the greatest part returned and restored the temple with heavy labour. But the ten tribes, which had less care for religion, because, the empire of the Chaldeans being destroyed, they lived freely under the kings of the Persians, when they learned that the temple was built and the envy of the Samaritans repressed, at length some of them returned; more remained there, whose progeny is said to be kept to this day in the same parts and to serve the nation of the Persians. And as Zorobabel and Jesus [Josue] signify Christ, who by his grace releases the captivity of the human race and builds his house in us by sanctifying and possessing it, so Esdras, the priest and ready scribe, figures the same [Christ], who came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it; who could therefore be called the scribe of the law or the ready scribe in the law of Moses, because he himself gave the law to Moses through the angel, he himself taught the prophets the truth, he himself kindles the minds of the elect to understand and do the will of the Father. Whence: "For this is the testament which I will make to the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord: I will give my laws into their mind" etc.; and: "My tongue is the pen of a scrivener" etc. For the tongue of the prophet was the pen of a ready scribe, because what the Lord taught him within without delay of time, this he himself declared outwardly in time through the office of the tongue. Esdras also is interpreted 'helper', because Christ alone frees his people from tribulations and leads them from the confusion of vices to the peace of the virtues by advancing steps of merits. Whence: "My help is from the Lord" etc. Moreover, as Esdras brought back no small part of the people from captivity to Jerusalem, and money and holy vessels for the glory of the temple, and purged the people of foreign wives by his pontifical authority, so Christ, appearing in the flesh, entered the confusion of the world free from the confusion of vices, that, returning, he might lead us with him, freed from all confusion, into the tranquillity of the peace above; whose pledge of peace we receive in the present, according to that: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you"; that is, I leave temporal [peace] to those on pilgrimage, I give perpetual [peace] to those who come to the heavenly homeland.
18_marg125: BEDE. On the first day of the month he began to go up from Babylon, and in the fifth, with the children of the transmigration, and on the first day of the month, he came to Jerusalem. For the beginning of the month, in which the moon is believed to borrow new light from the sun, signifies a new beginning of the heavenly gift; and well did Esdras go up from Babylon on the first day of the first month with those whom he was saving from captivity, because the beginning of the holy life, in which we renounce Satan and his kingdom, is brought about in us by the illumination of the divine goodness. On the first day of the fifth month too he came to Jerusalem, because this too comes about not by the freedom of our will but by the inspiration of the light above, that, having heard the gospel, we are incorporated in the members of the Church. And a beautiful and wholesome custom has grown up in the Church by the teaching of the fathers, that to those who are catechized the sacrament of the four gospels is explained and recited at the beginning. Again, he came on the first day of the fifth month to Jerusalem with those who had been freed from the enemies, because when, the precepts of the four gospels having been fulfilled, we enter the heavenly kingdom, we celebrate as it were a new beginning of the month, because we now behold the joys of new light in the sun of justice; as it were, after the four months of bright action which we have passed on the way, we spend the fifth month of everlasting reward in the light of the heavenly homeland.
18_marg126: In the first month Esdras began to go up from Babylon, and in the fifth he came with the children of the transmigration to Jerusalem. For four months complete the journey from Babylonia to Jerusalem, because through the four books of the gospel we learn the faith and the sacraments of truth, by which, rescued from the captivity of the devil with the Lord as leader, we ascend to the liberty of the sons of God; and in the same books are contained the precepts of works, by which as by daily steps we may come to the promises above.
18_marg127: Strengthened, that is, by the divine grace and protection by which he might prosperously finish what he had begun. So also Christ: because God "was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself", the hand of God too was upon his humanity, by which, exalted in the passion, he also ascended to the walls of the city above and opened the way to his faithful.
18_marg128: BUT ESDRAS etc. Great is the virtue of a man to prepare his heart for the service of the divine will, and to be able to say: "My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready" etc.
18_marg129: Christ too prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, because he divinely provided to take to himself such a manhood as should be not only without sin but also "full of grace and truth", which, with no law of sin resisting it, might keep the law of God without any contradiction of mind or flesh. Whence: "In the head of the book it is written of me" etc. Again, the Lord sought the law of God, because, casting away the traditions of the Pharisees, he taught to understand holy Scripture mystically, and showed that the decrees of the gospel which he brought were more perfect and acceptable to God than those which he had sent before through Moses. Whence: "You have heard that it hath been said to them of old: Thou shalt love thy neighbour [so the edition: 'amicum'], and hate thy enemy. But I say to you, Love your enemies" etc.
18_interl103: "Jesus began to do and to teach"
18_interl107: to distinguish him, namely, from those whom he knew to have been set up from dead men, or indeed from nothing
18_marg130: Artaxerxes, who with devout mind venerated the temple and the priests of the Lord and served him, signifies Christian princes, as Darius also does. Nor is it wonderful if the successors of Cyrus, who had the temple and the city built, who loved and helped his servants and the law, figure Christian kings, since the Lord himself said through the prophet that Cyrus signified his Son, and honoured him with his name, saying: "Thus saith the Lord to my anointed Cyrus."
18_marg131: Because the fame of the divine power had reached the king, through which he had renewed the law burnt by the Chaldeans in the same proper words as before, though in another character of letters.
18_marg132: He grants leave to go to all, he compels no one to go. Christian princes, compelling no one, lest the will of faith be uncertain, permit all whom it pleases to worship Christ in their kingdom.
18_marg133: AND HIS SEVEN COUNSELLORS. In the book of Esther we read that it was the custom of the kings of the Persians to use the counsel of seven in all things to be done or decided. The faithful use seven counsellors when in all that they do they follow the precepts of divine Scripture, of which it is said: "The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times", that is, perfected by the holy illumination of the sevenfold Spirit.
18_marg134: Esdras is sent from before the king and his seven counsellors to visit Judea and Jerusalem, when the princes of the world, converted to the faith and strengthened by the persuasions of the Scriptures, desire Christ to come to save the Church and gather it from the gentiles with daily help, which the name Esdras signifies, saying: "Turn again, O God of hosts, look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard" etc.
18_interl108: not only on the tongue, because "Jesus began to do and to teach"
18_marg135: It is wonderful that a phrase is found in the letter of Artaxerxes which the prophets are wont to use, when he says that the law of God is in the hand of his servant. For it is written: "The word of the Lord came by the hand of Aggeus the prophet", and: "The Lord hath done that which he spoke by the hand of his servant Elias", and: "The Lord testified to Israel and to Juda by the hand of all the prophets"; because, namely, the prophets preached the things of God no less by working than by speaking.
18_marg136: Christ had the law in his hand, because he once established it through Moses as he willed, and now, changing the same through himself, carried it over to more perfect things.
18_marg137: The faith and wisdom of the king and his counsellors are to be noted, who understood that their gifts were rather to be offered through him who had the law of God in his hand, that is, fulfilled it in work.
18_marg138: BEDE. Faithfully and learnedly he says that he has a tabernacle in Jerusalem whom he had called above the God of heaven. For we use a tabernacle on a journey, and the God of heaven has a tabernacle in Jerusalem because he who has an eternal seat in the heavens himself deigns to stay for a time with the saints on pilgrimage in this Church; whence: "Behold the tabernacle of God with men." And because Esdras bore the type not only of the preachers, of whom he was one, but also of Christ, to whose members he belonged, we offer gifts as it were through him when we need his aid in all things, that the good things we do may be acceptable to God the Father. "For no man", he says, "cometh to the Father, but by me." And of him Paul says: "He is the propitiation for our sins."
18_marg139: With this money the faithful desire their good works to shine in their Church, that through this they may have a part [so the edition: 'patrem'] with the saints, and others may profit by their examples. For as it were with our silver and gold sacrifices, libations and victims are bought to offer to the Lord, when our neighbours, seeing the brightness of our works, are converted to the office of piety, by which they too are consecrated to the Lord by living well. But there are certain most brilliant virtues of the saints which cannot be shown to all as examples of work, but only recited to glorify the grace of God; as is that Daniel and Jeremias prophesied as boys, that John [did so] not yet born, that Cornelius with his house received the Holy Spirit not yet baptized, and innumerable miracles, like silver in the house of the Lord. Nor can the offerings which are placed upon the altar be bought only from this silver or gold; because when we hear such things we ought indeed to wonder at them as divine, but we cannot imitate them as possible.
18_interl109: note that some priests remained in Babylonia with the rest of the people
18_interl110: for this reason the money was given
18_interl111: which, namely, were offered of the fruits of the earth, as bread and fine flour and ears of corn
18_marg140: The true Esdras delivered the vessels of mercy, which are delivered to him by men, in the sight of the Father into the Jerusalem above. Of which it is said: "How can any one enter into the house of the strong, and rifle his goods, unless he first bind the strong?" For the king of Babylon, that is, the devil, was strong, but, conquered and bound by the Lord, he lost the vessels which he possessed unjustly, that is, the hearts of the elect, nor could he oppose him who took them away and brought them back to the city above, whose own they were.
18_marg141: Christian princes command their subjects to give without delay whatever Christ our high priest has asked, holding back nothing at all: let them give gold in the confession of true faith, wheat in the showing of good working, wine in the fervour of love, oil in the cheerfulness of mercy; and all these are commanded to be given under the number of a hundred to the great priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven, that is, to Christ, who, bringing us heavenly commandments from the Father, has promised heavenly rewards in the Father's house to the obedient. For the hundred, which in counting on the fingers passes from the left hand to the right, designates the joys which are at the right hand of the Judge [so the edition: 'indicis'], that is, eternal life. And the talent is handed down as of threefold measure: the least of fifty pounds, the middle of seventy pounds, the greatest of a hundred and twenty pounds; the core thirty measures; the bate, which is also the ephi, the tenth part of the core, that is, three measures.
18_marg142: BEDE. Salt signifies wisdom, and hence in common speech the dull are called saltless. But it matters of what kind the salt is; for the Lord too commanded through the law that salt be offered with every sacrifice, and in the gospel says: "Have salt in you, and have peace among you." Yet not in vain is David read to have struck the Edomites in the Valley of saltpits; because, namely, we are commanded to offer in all the sacrifices of our works the salt of heavenly wisdom, with which catechumens are initiated; but David strikes the saltpit of the valleys with its inhabitants because Christ destroys weak and worldly wisdom with its followers. Hence it is well commanded that salt be given without measure diligently in the house of the God of heaven, because it is necessary that whatever wisdom anyone has, he should show it wholly in the service of God. But it is to be recalled that the Samaritans, writing to the other Artaxerxes, said above that, mindful of the salt which they had eaten in the palace, they could not bear the temple and city of God to be built against his advantage. But here Artaxerxes commands all the keepers of the public chest to give, among other things, salt as much as is needed in the house of God. For there it is known that heretics are animated to attack the Church by the fraudulent taste of human wisdom; but here, that the wise, converted to the faith, help the Church through the discipline of worldly wisdom, while through it they overcome the adversaries.
18_marg143: By this privilege it is shown that the rest of the common people of the children of Israel, on reaching the homeland, paid the king's tribute; which the king is known to have done with discerning foresight, that those who were occupied with the divine service should be free from his own service, and that no one should exact tribute from those who possessed nothing of their own in the land but lived on the tithes of the people. By all these things it is proved that he not only loved but also learned very well what the worship of the divine service required.
18_interl113: Artaxerxes plainly expresses what devotion kings would have in Christian times, or what they would do toward the faith of truth in all things
18_marg144: AND THOU etc. BEDE. The king repeats what he had said above, and confirms with repeated speech the truth which he knew. For above he said that [the law] was in the hand of Esdras, because the law of God is wisdom. Whence: "The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: and his tongue shall speak judgment. The law of his God is in his heart." And the just man has the law of God and wisdom in his hand when in all that he does and says he shows himself mindful of the divine will. Mystically, our Lord has wisdom in his hand, "for he is the power of God and the wisdom of God". He appoints judges, that is, the rulers of the churches, who judge all things according to his will and preach the faith to the unlearned throughout the world; and everyone who despises the decrees of his law will be punished either with present or with future punishment according to the measure of his sin. In these things Artaxerxes expressed what devotion kings would have in the future Christian times, and what they would do toward the faith of truth.
18_marg145: We can refer the person of Esdras also to any doctor of the Church, to whom kings and princes have often sent letters for the state of the faithful.
18_interl114: Esdras, having received the letter, broke forth into the praise of God
18_interl115: it is not to be doubted that the king's words are holy and mystical, which the prophet confirms were divinely inspired in him, [and] by which he shows also that the house of God was glorified
18_interl116: namely by the power by which he works all things
18_marg146: So each one who is made fit by his teaching to gather others must first [so the edition: 'debrius'] be strengthened in mind by the grace of God against all things that hinder the work of the saints.
18_marg147: He carefully enumerates the chiefs who went up with him from Babylon and unfolds their genealogy; he adds also their number, which came to one thousand four hundred and forty; hinting that the names of those who go up from the confusion of the world are written in the book of life, but that the doctors, that is, the chiefs of the families of the people of God, receive as much increase of everlasting reward as they gain souls for the Lord. Whence to the servant who says: "Thy pound hath gained ten pounds", it is answered: "Have thou power over ten cities"; that is, from the life of those whom thou hast taught thou shalt be more glorious in the kingdom of God.
18_marg148: BEDE. I do not remember having read the name of this place elsewhere. But since it is written in what follows: And I proclaimed there a fast by the river Hana on the tenth day of the first month, it seems that Hana is a river and that another river runs down into it, at whose meeting Esdras gathered the host. But Josephus puts the Euphrates; hence it seems that Hana is some stream of the Euphrates.
18_marg149: Fittingly, before he began so long a journey, he provided himself with a supply of ministers of the house of God, through whom, coming to Jerusalem, he might accomplish what was necessary for the uses of the temple.
18_marg150: BEDE. The Caspian Sea, according to Orosius, rises from the ocean under the northern quarter, along both shores of which near the ocean lie deserted and untilled places. From there it stretches toward the south through long narrows, until, widened over great spaces, it ends at the roots of the mountain. It has from the east to the ocean very many nations of the Hyrcanians and Scythians, wandering widely [so the edition: 'observantes'] because of the barrenness [so the edition: 'infusionem infecundam'] of the lands. On the west it has many nations, but in general the region, very large, of farther Albania under the Caspian sea and mountain is called [the region] of the Amazons. Where it is to be noted that, while the historians write Caspium, Esdras names it Casphia. For the Hebrews, not having the letter p, use ph instead of it in Greek or barbarian names, as Phetrus, Philatus. The children of Israel are therefore shown to have come into Casphia through the captivity of the Assyrians or Chaldeans, when Esdras sends there that ministers of the house of the Lord might be brought, namely Levites and Nathinites, whom Josephus names sacred servants. And it is to be noted that they lived in very free peace, though among foreigners, who were able at once to send so great a force. For their catalogue shows that there were two hundred and fifty-eight chosen men in that expedition; with whom added Esdras is found to have had in his host a sum of nearly one thousand seven hundred men.
18_marg151: BEDE. An example of fasting and praying is given us when we wish to begin anything of great virtue; and because faithful hope in the Lord is never deceived, nor can it be that what we justly seek from a pious helper by continence and prayer with faith we do not obtain. But it is to be noted that the fast is put first and the prayer follows. For first he says: And I proclaimed there a fast etc. Then he added: And that we might ask of him a right way. And in the conclusion of the sentence: And we fasted, and besought our God etc. For it behoves whoever comes to beseech the mercy of the Lord first to show himself worthy to be heard by living more continently, and so to pray and not doubt that what he asks will turn out prosperously.
18_marg152: BEDE. By the silver and gold vessels which are sent from Babylon to Jerusalem are signified the souls which are converted from the confusion of the world to the Lord. Hence well does Esdras the keeper commend the vessels to the priests, to carry them to Jerusalem; because whoever desire to attain to the fellowship of the Church are washed in baptism by the priests and consecrated to the Lord; and through them are reconciled by repenting those who had departed from the Church by sinning and, by persevering in sins, had fallen into the service of the devil, as into the captivity of the Babylonian king. And well are there twelve priests to whom this care is committed, because of the twelve apostles, through whose teaching the Church was first founded and through whose successors it is to be built up to the end.
18_marg153: There is a difference between these vessels which Esdras offers with the priests at Jerusalem and those which Zorobabel and Jesus [Josue] are related to have offered; because those were carried from the temple of the Lord into Babylon and afterwards brought back to Jerusalem, but these were made in Babylonia and sent to Jerusalem by way of devotion by the king or the princes of the Persians, or even by the people of Israel who dwelt in those parts. Those vessels therefore signify those who, after receiving the knowledge and the sacraments of the faith, after beginning the works of the virtues, are deceived by the devil and snatched into his confusion, but are called back to salvation by the grace of Christ; but these, those who, born with the sin of the first transgression, expiated through the laver of regeneration by the ministry of the priests, are joined to the children of the Church.
18_marg154: YOU ARE THE HOLY ONES OF THE LORD. The doctors of the Church must never forget holiness, because they have been consecrated by the Lord through the Holy Spirit unto the day of redemption, to the receiving of which they should also train their hearers; that those who have already been offered to the Lord through the rudiments of the faith may be further confirmed by the examples and admonitions of those who have gone before in the faith, and be made worthy of entrance into the city above.
18_marg155: The priests must watch lest any of the souls entrusted to them, that is, the vessels of the Lord, perish; but [let them] be brought in their full number to the buildings of holy virtue.
18_marg156: That is, that you present those whom the providence above has committed to you, by instructing and teaching them, such as may be found irreproachable and fit for the treasury of the heavenly hall, that is, for the seats of inner peace and light; and this not by the judgment of any who can be deceived, but of the apostles and of those who are to judge with the Lord. For these are rightly understood [to be] the chiefs of the priests and Levites and the heads of the families of Israel, that is, of men or souls seeing God; of whom it is said: "Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth"; and elsewhere: "Her husband is honourable in the gates" etc.
18_marg157: BEDE. All things are full of mysteries. For above we read that on the first day of the month they began to go up from Babylon; now it is said that on the tenth [so the edition] day of the same month they set forward from the river Hana. On the first day of the month, therefore, they went out of the gates of Babylonia, but waited by the aforesaid river until the twelfth day, until the Levites and Nathinites came from Casphia, and they commended themselves to the Lord by fasting and praying the longer because of the dangers of the long journey. And we too, when we teach new peoples of the Church to renounce the devil and to believe in and confess the true God, go out from Babylon as it were at the beginning of the first month with money to be consecrated to the Lord, because we hand on the beginning of a new conversion to those whom, rescued from the devil, we lead to the heavenly kingdom. Hence the same month is called [the month] of new things or of new fruits. For in it, for the same signification of new life, the fathers were led out of Egypt. And when we hand on to the hearers of the new life the creed of faith, which was ordained by the twelve apostles and comprised in as many sentences, we stay as it were twelve days in the first station, and so undertake the journey begun to the land of promise; because after the knowledge of faith has been received we show them that the way of the virtues, by which one comes to life, must be entered on. In which days Esdras with the children of the transmigration was given to fasts and prayers and to the gathering of the Levites and Nathinites; because when we gain new peoples of the faith we must most of all strive after the virtues, by which we may commend ourselves more familiarly to the Lord and offer those whom we instruct an example of good work; we call also a religious band of brethren to our help, aided by which we may more effectively carry over the souls of the faithful to the society of the elect and the citadel of the more perfect life, as holy vessels to the temple of the Lord.
18_marg158: Three days are spent in Jerusalem, which are three virtues, faith, hope and charity; these the doctors must first show in themselves, and so offer those whom they have taught and trained in the same virtues to the fathers who went before in Christ to be tested. For when the Church finds those whom we catechize upright in faith and action, it is as if, weighing what we offer in the temple by the hand of the priests, it found it of pure metal and perfect weight; which is done daily in this Church through the elect in examining the life of believers, and is more perfectly fulfilled in the Jerusalem above in those who deserve to enter. For in this life the doctors, as it were staying three days in Jerusalem, on the fourth day offer to the priests to be weighed the silver and gold which they had offered, when they show themselves strong in faith, lofty in hope, fervent in devotion, and show that their hearers shine through the confession of right faith as tried silver, gleam through purity of sense [so the edition: 'immolati'] as the finest gold, and stand out as consecrated vessels through the receiving of spiritual gifts. In the homeland above too, when they receive the grace of reward for faith, hope and charity, and afterwards also for those whom they have taught, it is as if after the joy of the three days' stay in Jerusalem they were honoured the more for the gifts and precious vessels which they offered.
18_marg159: BEDE. This is done when the doctors carefully examine the life of their subjects, namely how far each has advanced in faith or working, that they may order them according to the measure of their capacity in competent grades in the house of the Lord. But if the one set over them is sluggish through idleness, and either does not know the life of his subjects or pretends not to know it, the inner Judge, who keeps the number of believers and the weight of each in the balance of his examination, "will render to every man according to his works". It can also be said that, when the prelates come to the Jerusalem above, [all] is written down, when every work of good action of those whom they had instructed is at that time [written] in the book of life and given worthy recompense in heaven.
18_marg160: BEDE. Great devotion and religion is shown when, coming to the temple, first of all they offer holocausts, not only for themselves but also for all Israel, that is, for those who had already returned home and for those who were still in exile. Mystically, those truly and perfectly escaped by repenting the captivity of the devil, in which they were held by sinning, who subject themselves with fixed intention to the divine service, who, drawn wholly away from lowest things, kindle themselves with the flame of heavenly desire. For this is to offer holocausts, that is, wholly burnt sacrifices, to the Lord: to think or do nothing in all things but his will.
18_marg161: Not only for himself. It is the sign of a perfect mind when one sacrifices for all Israel, that is, for the general safety of the faithful, beseeching the pity above as one mindful of unity and brotherhood.
18_interl118: they honoured [them] by the royal authority with which Esdras had been raised up
18_marg162: By adorning it more grandly with divers gifts which the king and his counsellors and princes had sent, and by freeing its ministers and priests from all straits. Mystically, the people and the temple of God hold one and the same figure of the Church, which Esdras and the children of the transmigration lift up, the sacred vessels having been brought from Babylon, when preachers, joining to it with the Lord's help new peoples of believers, show it honourable and terrible to all. The same, when they advance or carry forward those whom they have trained by examples in good conversation or by words even to the receiving of the heavenly rewards, lift up the people into the house of God, because they make great joy both to the elect who abide in the homeland above and to those still on pilgrimage on earth.
18_interl119: who, namely, had come with Esdras
18_marg163: AFTER etc. BEDE. This transgression is plainly described in the prophet Malachias and rebuked by prophetic authority: namely that, returned from the captivity, both the princes and priests and Levites and the rest of the people cast off their Israelite wives, who, worn out by poverty and the toil of the journey and the frailty of their sex, were weakened and disfigured, and married foreign women in the flower of their age, either more beautiful or daughters of the powerful and rich. Which is to be understood not of those who had then come with Esdras, but of those who had long since gone up from the captivity with Zorobabel and Jesus [Josue]. For those who had come with Esdras could not so soon despise the teaching of so great a leader as, having not yet stayed five months in the homeland, to leave their wives and take foreign [so the edition: 'eternas'] ones; of whose number the princes are understood to have been who, reporting this crime to Esdras, took care to correct it.
18_marg164: It is to be noted that the princes strive to correct the sins which the princes committed and made the people committed to them commit; but because they cannot by themselves, they refer the case to the chief, that is, the archbishop, by whose authority the crime may be expiated. Mystically, the foreign wives signify heresies and the superstitious sects of the philosophers, which, when they are incautiously admitted into the Church, contaminate with error the holy seed of catholic truth and pure action. All the sins too with which the heathen are polluted, when Christians are not ashamed to imitate them, [make them] as it were through foreign wives degenerate from the seed of the word of God, by which they had been begotten, according to that: "Of his own will hath he begotten us by the word of truth" etc.; and as it were they beget profane offspring of the daughters of foreigners, when, following the allurements of those who err, they bring forth perverse acts from them to the notice of all.
18_marg165: It is to be noted that, Israel, that is, the ten tribes, having been carried away into captivity, the two tribes, that is, Juda and Benjamin, are called Israel indifferently by the former name. The people of Israel therefore are not here called the ten tribes to distinguish them from Juda and Benjamin; but to distinguish them from the peoples of the lands the people of God in general is understood, which polluted the dignity of the heavenly name by fellowship with the earthly. Hence in Malachias, whom the Hebrews think to be Esdras: "Juda hath transgressed, and abomination hath been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem" etc.; where, saying Juda, he plainly signifies that the people of the first transgression was polluted in this. And what he adds: "The Lord will cut off the master and the scholar" etc., shows that the princes and the people were polluted and were to be rooted out from the fellowship of the saints unless they repented. And what he joins: "Offering gifts to the Lord of hosts", warns them that they offer to the Lord in vain who do not fear to subject themselves to the devil.
18_marg166: Wonderful is the faith of the princes and people rescued from the captivity, who, being the holy seed, call the other nations the peoples of the lands, to signify that, though created of earth, they dwell in heaven, while they believe above others in the God of heaven and hope to obtain heavenly benefits from him; whence rightly they grieve that their sanctification has been defiled by the abominations of the nations, and, what is graver, confess that the princes who ought to have corrected [it] were the first to err.
18_interl121: of catholic truth and pure action
18_interl122: signifying the grief of his heart by a mourning habit, that, namely, he might the more quickly stir the minds of all to penance
18_interl126: which is the token of the male sex and age, and is therefore put in the designation of the virtues
18_interl127: teaching that pardon is to be obtained through the laments of penance
18_marg167: BEDE. By garments are wont to be designated works, with which we are clothed to glory if they are clean, or to shame if unclean. By the hairs of the head, thoughts, which rise from the hidden root of the heart as from the inner roots of the brain; which, if they are right, ought to be kept, but if reprobate, cut off. Hence of Samuel, who was to be holy, his mother says: "And no razor shall come upon his head." And the Lord says to the apostles: "A hair of your head shall not perish"; because all the thoughts of the saints are in eternal memory with God. But the sinner, that he may be cleansed from his iniquities, must cast away reprobate thoughts, namely the origin of evil works. Hence the leper in Leviticus, his health being recovered, is commanded among the other purifications to shave all the hairs of his flesh, that, so expiated with victims, he may deserve to enter the camp; because then at last are we perfectly cleansed from vices when we drive out even harmful thoughts. The beard too, the token of the male sex and age, is wont to signify virtue. The high priest therefore rent his mantle and coat, to signify that his subjects had works less perfect, which needed to be rent from their solidity by penance and renewed into a better habit; he plucked the hairs of his head, that they might root out wicked thoughts from the heart and give place to useful ones about to be born. He plucked also the hairs of his beard, that they might be humbled in the very virtues which they seemed to have, and might remember that those which were mixed with vices were small or nothing in the examination of the eternal Judge. He sat mourning, to teach that pardon is to be merited through the laments of penance.
18_marg168: Note how much the examples of the doctors help: Esdras is written to have said nothing, but only, on hearing of the crime, to have wept, and to have drawn the crowd of the faithful to himself not by shouting but by weeping.
18_marg169: THERE WERE ASSEMBLED etc. A great change of affairs: through the faithlessness of the princes many had followed luxury; [now,] while the great prince mourns and hints what sinners must do, all who fear the word of God, by which he threatens that transgressors are to be punished, come together to him.
18_interl128: "The lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice"
18_interl129: namely, the flesh of Christ on the cross
18_marg170: BEDE. Typically, that, having rent his garment, he bends his knees and spreads out his hands to God, and, pouring out prayers and tears, turns the minds of very many to penance, shows Christ, who prayed for our sins before the passion and in it, and who, with his hands stretched out on the cross, willed the garment of his flesh to be rent with wounds and put to death; whence: "He died for our sins" etc. Which was fittingly done at the time of the evening sacrifice; either because the Lord at the end offered [the sacrament] of flesh and blood to the Father and commanded us to offer it in bread and wine; or because, as the legal sacrifice came to its end, he freed us by his passion and, separating us from the peoples of the lands, made us heavenly, and commanded us to cleave to him chaste in heart and body. His very prayer too, in which, being just, he associates himself with the sinful people, saying: My God, I am confounded etc., fits the humility of the Redeemer, who appeared in the likeness of sinful flesh to take away sin; whence: "O God my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Far from my salvation." Again: "O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee." Not that he could have offences or foolishness in himself, who "of God is made unto us wisdom, and justice, and sanctification, and redemption"; but, taking upon himself the [nature] of those whom he had come to save, he mercifully deigned to transfer to himself also those things which truly belonged to their frailty.
18_marg171: I BOWED MY KNEES etc. He prepared himself by compunction of heart and affection of body, that he might be made worthy to be heard by the pity above, and broke forth into these words of prayer. And he bends his knees, spreads out his hands and pours forth prayers at the time of the evening sacrifice, knowing that what is done in the spirit of humility and with a contrite mind is more pleasing than what is offered with the flesh and blood of cattle.
18_interl130: Christ too prayed for us, saying: "O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee"
18_interl131: namely of the rulers of this darkness
18_interl134: because the spiritual "wolf catcheth and scattereth the sheep"
18_interl141: "The land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice"
18_interl143: that it might be fulfilled, namely, in work
