18_interl146: with the people of these abominations
18_interl151: the fruit, namely, of the prayer and lamentation of Esdras
18_marg172: Those, namely, who had sinned, doing penance, or those who had remained in chastity, grieving at the fall of their brethren. And they are shown to have been much troubled at the prayers and laments of their high priest, since women and children too are related to have been present. And it can be understood to have been done with this distinction: that first the innocent and upright flocked to him, when he says: "And there were assembled to me all that feared the word of the God of Israel" etc.; but now those also who had sinned came together with their wives and children to do penance.
18_marg173: OF THE SONS OF ELAM etc. Josephus says that this was the first of the people of Jerusalem, who, as befits a prince, at once helped the intention of Esdras with the greatest authority, by confessing that the people had sinned with him and by urging penance, the foreign wives with their children being cast off.
18_marg174: AND NOW IF THERE BE REPENTANCE etc. As if [to say]: If the people perfectly repents of this sin, let us first, turned to the Lord, promise amendment and ask pardon; then, returning to ourselves, let us root out every root of the sin and its shoot, namely by casting out the wives with all their offspring. For this is truly to do penance: to be turned to the Lord with the whole heart and within, and to cut off outwardly all matter of sinning from its very origin.
18_marg175: He teaches fittingly how one should act in counsel with superiors: namely that each should say according to his own sense what he has understood, or seems to himself to have understood, to be best, and yet leave to him who presides the place of deciding, ready to obey all that he shall decree is to be done according to the will and law of God.
18_marg176: Who was then high priest; after Jesus the son of Josedec, Joachim his son, and after him Eliasib his son held the high priesthood.
18_marg177: BEDE. The priests have here an example not only of weeping and praying but also of fasting for those who have sinned. For blessed are they who mourn their own sins, because, having received remission, they are comforted; but more blessed are they who weep for the sins of others, so that they will not touch even bread and water, which is the refreshment of the abstinent, nor enter their house or go up into the bed of their couch, but pass the night praying in the courts of the house of the Lord. For there was the house of the priest which Esdras is said to have entered when evening came on. And another edition, for 'the chamber of Johanan', has 'the pastophorium of Johanan', by which name is often called the porch by which the temple is surrounded on every side, in which the ministers and keepers of the temple stayed. They mourn too now at the transgression of those who had come from the captivity, who grieve that those who had been rescued from sins by repenting have relapsed into them by sinning and have been as it were taken captive again by the devil. Of whose seducers, as of the parents of the unclean wives, Peter says: "For, speaking proud words of vanity, they allure by the desires of fleshly riotousness those who for a little while escape." And a little after: "For if, flying from the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Jesus Christ, they be again entangled in them and overcome: their latter state is become unto them worse than the former."
18_marg178: BEDE. Which by the Hebrews is called Casleu, by the Romans December, which is in the middle of winter, rainy and stormy. Hence it is to be noted that, when the people came together in the middle of winter, they are recorded as trembling because of the sin and because of the rains. For when they saw the rains greater than usual even in the very season of rains, returning to their conscience they imputed this to their sins and feared wrath from the very disturbance of the air; therefore they did not presume to do their business in private houses, but sat in the street of the house of the Lord, having put on the habit of penance and humility. This [is said] because of those who, when the elements are disturbed and the cold of the winds, or floods of rain, or heaps of snow, or the heat of drought, or even the destruction of men or animals weighs down from above, and the Judge himself shows the force of his wrath even by open signs, seek nothing of amendment of manners by which they may appease the Judge and escape the impending blow, but with worldly pride consider by what art they may either avoid or overcome the adversities which rage outwardly because of their sins.
18_marg179: BEDE. That is, around the court of the priests, by which the house itself was surrounded on every side, having round about it on every side, in a square, very spacious buildings of courts, in which the people too, when there was need because of rain, could stand and see the things that were done at the doors of the temple, or around the temple; for they had the inner walls next the ground made on columns, the outer ones solid.
18_marg180: BEDE. This place answers to what was said above: And Esdras rose up before the house of God, and went to the chamber of Johanan the son of Eliasib etc. Where the devotion of the high priest is to be noted, who, mourning, praying and fasting for the transgression of the people, remained in the courts of the temple, and would not enter his own house before, having received the consent of the people, he saw them penitent with their whole heart and converted to the Lord. Of which devotion the rest of the princes too seem to have been partners, when they are said themselves to have gone away, the synod being ended, into the houses of their fathers. For if Scripture does not signify this, what need was there to write that, the meeting being finished, Esdras and the heads of families went away from the enclosures of the temple into the houses of their fathers? For there is no one who does not know that they did this. What need was there to add: and all by their names, since this too was most well known to all, unless because it wished them to be understood as such men whose names and deeds should rightly be held in memory and handed on to posterity to be known?
18_marg181: AND THEY SAT etc. BEDE. Note that the number three is mystical. Above it was said that in three days all came together in Jerusalem, and now in three months, namely the tenth, eleventh and twelfth, they are cleansed from the foreign wives. For there are three virtues without which no one is saved: faith, hope and charity. In the third time of the world Christ, coming in the flesh into the world, bestowed on us the grace of the gospel. For he sent before the first time, before the law, in the patriarchs, the second under the law in the prophets; in the third he himself came with grace and, redeeming us by his passion, rose on the third day. Since by his grace we are joined to the fellowship of the Church and purged from the allurements of vices, fittingly the children of the transmigration came in three days to be cleansed and completed the cleansing in three months. According to the letter too they laboured opportunely, that before the beginning of the first month they might all be purged, that they might celebrate the Pasch and the very month in which it was to be celebrated cleanly and holily, and begin and finish the year cleanly and holily. Which it behoves us too to imitate every year in the Lent of the Pasch, that, the Lord's resurrection being at hand, "we may cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit", that we may be able to be partakers of the resurrection.
18_marg182: BEDE. The Hebrews fit to this place that of the prophet Zacharias: "And the Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord: and Satan stood on his right hand to be his adversary." And a little after: "And Jesus was clothed with filthy garments: and he stood before the face of the angel. Take away the filthy garments from him. And he said to him: Behold I have taken away thy iniquity, and have clothed thee with change of garments. And he said: Put a clean mitre upon his head." Rightly, they say, "Satan stood on his right hand to be his adversary", because the accusation was true, for he himself with the rest married a foreign wife. And what is said, that "Jesus was clothed with filthy garments", they interpret in three ways: either because of the unlawful marriage, or because of the sins of the people, or because of the squalor of the captivity. And the angel before whose face Jesus stood commanded the other angels to take away from him the filthy garments. Which done, the same angel said: "Behold I have taken away thy iniquity from thee"; these are the filthy garments; "and have clothed thee with change of garments", that is, I have joined to thee an Israelite wife. And what follows: "Put a clean mitre upon his head", they will have to be understood of the dignity of the priesthood, because, namely, the filth of sins being taken away, he had a clean priesthood. But it is to be observed that Esdras does not write that Jesus married a foreign wife, but some of his sons and brethren etc.
18_marg183: BEDE. Kinsmen, that is; for his brothers german in the flesh could not still live and give themselves to pleasure, since a hundred years and more had passed since Cyrus, beginning to reign, sent back Jesus and Zorobabel with the transmigration of Juda and Benjamin to Jerusalem to build the house of the Lord.
18_marg184: AND THEY GAVE etc. BEDE. First they cast off the unlawful wives, and so offer a ram for themselves, that, the crime being taken away, they might come clean to the altar. For it is hard for the victim of one to be acceptable to God who has not first left the fault for which he offers; whence: "Cease to do perversely, learn to do well." And because those who had sinned first were sons or brethren of the high priest, rightly in amendment of the crime they offer a ram of the flocks, to signify that they had resolved to slay themselves, who seemed to be leaders of the people as leaders of the flock, from their former life, and, purged by worthy penance, to offer themselves to God through a better life.
18_marg185: BEDE. Note with how great art of fighting the devil attacks the faithful, so as to leave them no time secure. For behold, those who could not be overcome by adversaries were conquering the public enemies, the temple of the Lord being built and dedicated, but were conquered by love of women, so as not to keep the temples of their hearts or works worthy of God. The figure of which thing is plainly fulfilled in our times, when we see the minds of the faithful now tempted much more dangerously within, drawn away and enticed by their own concupiscence, than they were once tempted without, when the savage adversary raged against their constancy with iron and fire. But the pity of the Lord will be present, which, as it gave the virtue of patience [so the edition: 'pentientie'] against the open struggles of the raging, so will give us the guard of caution against the snares of stealthy flatteries. Finally, by the diligence of the high priest bringing this about, those who feared the Lord "were all compunct in heart", those who had sinned also cast out the foreign wives; and so, the foulness of luxury being expelled, the beauty of chastity returned, and in the city of the Lord, the rubbish of vices being cast out, the flowers and ornaments of the virtues were scattered.
18_marg186: If anyone objects that it is not written that they cast out the sons of the adulteresses, but only the women themselves, although above, when Sechenias suggested and said: Let us make a covenant with the Lord our God, to put away all the wives, and such as are born of them, it was at once added: Then Esdras arose, and made the chiefs of the priests and of the Levites and all Israel swear that they would do according to this word, and they swore; let him understand that, if they did not cast out the sons, the reason was that they taught them to renounce their mothers' unbelief and, consecrated to the Lord by circumcision and the saving victim, joined them to their own faith and chastity. Mystically, the good works which we do with an eye to temporal advantage or favour or delight are either to be reckoned among evils, or to be separated from the low intention and done for the heavenly reward alone. For he who fasts, prays and gives alms that he may be seen and praised by men, such offspring of good action is born as it were of an unclean mother, and therefore cannot have a part among those who went up from Babylon to Jerusalem. For he who receives his reward in the present will lack it in the future, unless the author of the work, turning his mind to better things, begins to do for God what he was doing for empty praise, and, consecrating as it were the offspring unworthily brought forth to the Lord, makes it a citizen of Jerusalem, so that, correcting the work ill begun, he makes it worthy of everlasting reward in heaven.
